# Backlash Inspection

NOTE: To prevent damage to the inboard joint, always use soft jaws or equivalent materials between the inboard joint and a bench vise.

1. Install the driveshaft inboard joint and the intermediate shaft into the differential assembly.

2. Secure the driveshaft inboard joint (A) in a bench vise (B) with soft jaws (C).

![](images/533d38ba3c593858fc600364bd29017259733eeee8fd4001b428d027e470b6df.webp)

3. Place the intermediate shaft (D) on a V-block (E), then hold the intermediate shaft using locking pliers (F).

4. Measure the backlash of the final driven gear (G) using a dial indicator (H).

Standard: 1.4—2.0 mm (0.055— 0.079 in)

If the backlash is within the standard, go to step 5. If the backlash is out of the standard, replace the differential assembly.

5. Remove the driveshaft inboard joint from the bench vise.

6. Remove the driveshaft and the intermediate shaft from the differential assembly.

NOTE: Make sure the driveshaft inboard joint and the inboard boot are not damaged. If any damage is found, replace the driveshaft inboard joint or the inboard boot as an assembly.

# Differential Carrier, Final Driven Gear, and Transfer Drive Gear Replacement

NOTE: Inspect and adjust the bearing preload whenever the carrier is replaced.

1. If necessary, remove the carrier bearings (A) (see page 14-330).

![](images/4b7e7a9e7eb4e29b1f4c85c9667724a16375516638c0effe2c2c29ca3cb18f79.webp)

2. Remove the final driven gear (B) and the transfer drive gear (C) from the differential carrier (D).

NOTE: The final driven gear bolts (E) have left-hand threads.   
3. Replace the differential carrier or the final driven gear.   
4. Install the final driven gear on the differential carrier in the direction shown.   
5. Install the bolts through the differential carrier to the transfer drive gear.   
6. Tighten the bolts to the specified torque in a crisscross pattern in at least two steps.   
7. If you removed the carrier bearing for the differential carrier replaced, install the carrier bearings (see page   
14-330); replace it if it is damaged.

# Differential Carrier and Final Driven Gear Replacement

NOTE: Inspect and adjust the carrier bearing preload whenever the differential carrier is replaced.

1. If necessary, remove the carrier bearings (A) (see page 14-330).

![](images/1cf909d31611a87a36fc0d9c685450aeaac8e75a8b11761ed1337f6549f93b16.webp)

2. Remove the final driven gear (B) from the differential carrier (C). NOTE: The final driven gear bolts (D) have left-hand threads.   
3. Replace the differential carrier or the final driven gear.   
4. Instal the final driven gear on the differential carrier in the direction shown.   
5. Tighten the bolts to the specified torque in a crisscross pattern in at least two steps.   
6. If you removed the carrier bearing for the differential carrier replaced, instal the carrier bearings (see page   
14-330); replace it if it is damaged.

Special Tools Required Installer Attachment, 45 x 55 mm 07MAD-PR90100

# NOTE:

The carrier bearing and the bearing outer race should be replaced as a set.   
•Inspect and adjust the carrier bearing preload whenever the carrier bearing is replaced.   
Check the carrier bearing for wear and rough rotation. If the carrier bearing is OK, removal is not ñecessary.   
1. Remove the carrier bearing (A) with a commercially available bearing puller (B), a bearing separator (C), and a spacer (D).

![](images/28b970f5629f33754355684308b9fefbc6a347679f1a7db61a5f79cf1c09af6c.webp)

# NOTE:

1. Remove the bearing outer race (A), the spacer (B), and the 85 mm thrust shim (C) from the transmission housing (D) by heating the transmission housing to about 212 °F (100 °C) using a heat gun (E). Do not heat the transmission housing more than 212 °F (100 °C).

NOTE: Let the transmission housing cool to room temperature before installing a new bearing outer race.

If the transmission housing, the torque converter   
housing, the differential carrier, the carrier bearing, the bearing outer race, or the 85 mm thrust shim were replaced, the carrier bearing preload must be adjusted.

. Remove the bearing outer race (A), the spacer (B), and the 85 mm thrust shim (C) from the transmission housing (D) by heating the transmission housing to about 212 °F (100 °C) using a heat gun (E). Do not heat

# Carrier Bearing Preload Inspection (cont'd)

8. Measure the starting torque of the differential assembly using the preload inspection tool, a torque wrench (A), and a socket (B). Measure the starting torque at normal room temperature in both directions.

Standard   
New Bearing:   
3.9—5.1 N·m (40—52 kgf·cm, 35— 45 Ibf.in)   
Reused Bearing:   
3.6— 4.8 N·m (37 —49 kgf·cm, 32— 43 Ibf.in)

![](images/153b115f76d2876431cb8888374587dabaf0841b5a3fdede3f347189f97b71a7.webp)

9. If the starting torque is out of the standard, remove the 85 mm thrust shim and select a new 85 mm thrust shim from the following table. Install a new 85 mm thrust shim, and recheck. To increase the starting torque, increase the thickness of the 85 mm thrust shim. To decrease the starting torque, decrease the thickness of the 85 mm thrust shim.

Changing the 85 mm thrust shim to the next size will increase or decrease the starting torque about 0.5 — 0.6 N·m (5—6 kgf·cm, 5—5 Ibf.in)

# Transfer Output Shaft Installation Height Inspection/Adjustment

NOTE: If the transfer output shaft, the transfer output shaft bearing, the transmission housing bearing, the transmission housing, or the torque converter housing were replaced, adjust the transfer output shaft installation height with the 28.5 mm thrust shim.

1. Install the transfer output shaft (A) in the torque converter housing, and install the 28.5 mm thrust shim (B) on the top of the shaft. If you replace the 28.5 mm thrust shim with a new one, use the same thickness shim as the old one.

Standard: 46.31—46.35 mm (1.8232— 1.8248 in)

![](images/bb549ac38e2f2fcec95eff9ec3644e256584aa001fcf7830113586dd7059c48e.webp)  
Transfer Output Shaft Cutaway View

![](images/3242b790f3338d1ba5dcdb5040800957425b4663da04ad027d0b82e876e1d7ac.webp)

2. Install a new gasket (C) on the torque converter housing.

3. Measure the height (D) of the transfer output shaft installation between the surface (E) of the gasket and the top (F) of the 28.5 mm thrust shim in at least three places. Use the average as the actual height.

4. If the measurement is out of the standard, remove the 28.5 mm thrust shim and measure its thickness. 5. Select and install a new 28.5 mm thrust shim, then recheck the installation height.

THRUST SHIM, 28.5 mm

# Transfer Assembly Fluid Replacement

1. Warm up the engine to normal operating temperature (the radiator fan comes on), then turn the engine off.   
2. Raise the vehicle on a lift, and make sure it is securely supported.   
3. Remove the drain plug (A), and drain the transfer fluid (hypoid gear oil).

![](images/a09d2bdda6b969cf72d34042532937471f82800c927e6a140fcae36449e3f092.webp)

4. Reinstall the drain plug with a new sealing washer (B).

![](images/8b55d80b9d314ffaf147424a21e424b025175fd5d37d94defbed0d4b6d35cbb8.webp)

6. Refill the transfer assembly with the recommended fluid (hypoid gear oil) through the filler hole (C) until the fluid flows out. Use a SAE 90 viscosity hypoid gear oil, API classified GL4 or GL5 only.

Viscosity: SAE 90

Transfer Fluid (Hypoid Gear Oil) Capacity: 0.41 L (0.43 US qt) at change 0.45 L (0.48 US qt) at overhaul

7. Install the filler plug with a new sealing washer.

# Transfer Gear Backlash Measurement on Vehicle

1. Raise the vehicle on a lift, and make sure it is supported securely.   
2. Move the shift lever to N.   
3. Make a reference mark (A) across the No. 1 propeller shaft (B) and the transfer companion flange (C).

![](images/c6b164888f31022854b62ff9947885357295d9baf27dfabd6eb10a97a5f77a32.webp)

4. Separate the No.1 propeller shaft from the transfer companion flange.

5. Set a dial indicator (A) on the transfer companion flange (B); position the dial indicator tip (C) on the direct extension of the bolt hole center (D).

![](images/864ba905c3f48f2e1110d6c6d8482353c03879add7753fdeec6319f7a970df59.webp)

6. Measure the transfer gear backlash.

Standard: 0.06—0.16 mm (0.0024—0.0063 in)

If the backlash is out of the standard, replace the transfer assembly. If the backlash is within the standard, and the inspection is complete, go to step 7.

7. Install the No. 1 propeller shaft (A) to the transfer companion flange (B) by aligning the reference mark (C).

![](images/fcf287458c0efbc8771b68b83402d1a219386920da25fa86d903a731a83815fa.webp)

# Total Starting Torque Measurement

NOTE: To prevent damaging the transfer housing, always use wood blocks or equivalent materials between the transfer housing and the bench vise.

1. Remove the transfer assembly (see page 14-346). 2. Secure the transfer housing (A) in a bench vise (B) with soft jaws.

![](images/63b13f85609e8b4ee7d76d6f22be48eb8427ce6a854ede530a6dcc10b6d347d7.webp)

1. Check for fluid leaks between the mating surfaces of the transfer assembly and the transmission. If there is a leak, remove the transfer cover, then replace the transfer cover oil seal and the O-ring (see page 14-355).   
2. Check for fluid leaks between the transfer companion flange and the transfer oil seal. If there is a leak, replace the transfer oil seal and O-ring (see page 14-351). Do not replace the oil seal with the transfer assembly on the transmission.

3. Rotate the transfer companion flange several times to seat the tapered roller bearings.

4. Measure the total starting torque at the companion flange (C) using a torque wrench (D) and a socket (E).

Standard: 2.38—4.01 N-m (24.3—40.9 kgf·cm, 21.1 — 35.5 Ibf•in)

If the total starting torque is out of the standard, replace the transfer assembly.   
If the total starting torque is within the standard, go to step 5.

5. Install the transfer assembly (see page 14-347).

# System Description

The rear diffrential has a real-time 4WD control mechanism that enables 4WD by transmitting appropriate driving force from the front wheels to the rear wheels when necessary. It uses a real-time 4WD dual pump system (DPS) with a light and compact cam mechanism, and integrates the drive control system to the rear differential.

Equipped with a cam mechanism, this DPS real-time 4WD detects the speed difference between the front and the rear wheels. When speed difference is small the one-way cam works to minimize the possility of the pump to produce hydraulic pressure.

When the speed difference is large, hydraulic pressure develops in the two pumps. By controlling the engagement of the main clutch, the driving force transmitted to the rear wheels is optimized according to the driving conditions. By using alimiter switch to prevent transmission of excessive torque to the rear whees, the propeller shaft and differential unit can be lightweight and compact. For the rear differential fluid, DPFI (dual pump fluid Il is exclusively used.

![](images/2b574aedc2455dc891ebd86fa8fbd3c93532990cf8cd2eec06cc01e02a758631.webp)

# TORQUE TRANSFERRED TO THE REAR WHEELS

![](images/55abb077ad1e20df49cce5a90553f950c92b82038b222627447a5d7df41a6fe4.webp)

# One-Way Cam Operation

The one-way cam unit consists of two cams (front wheel and rear wheel) and balls between the two cams detects the difference in the front and rear wheel speeds.

When a difference of the front and rear wheel speeds develops, the difference in the rotational speed of the two cams also develops, and the front cam rotational speed exceeds that of the rear cam. When this happens, the balls move along the cam groove, pushes and widens the cams, and applies pressure to the main clutch. When the speed difference becomes greater, the dual pump system (DPS) operates. Since the cam unit is a one-way type, i only operates when driving forward.

# NORMAL DRIVING:

![](images/2f7717096985aae582301e3a7bd4073d9fe128d9e8cb370eb5caa270e7a85b92.webp)

# For non-slippery roads (no slipping): DPS not operating

When the front and the rear wheel speeds are equal no slipping) as in normal driving, the oil discharged from the front pump and the oil drawn in the rear pump are equal,so the hydraulic pressure that pushes the wet-type multi-plate clutch is not developed, and the rear wheels are not driven.

![](images/8da8cc51f0830e3463f68b6098c7c3cb0a2298ba800a60bafce944f2a72956d1.webp)

# For slippery roads (with slipping): DPS operating

When the front wheel speed is more than the rear wheel speed such as in starting, acceleration, and driving on a slippery road surface, the amount of oil discharged by the front pump exceeds the oil drawn by the rear pump, thus producing hydraulic pressure that engages the wet-type multi-plate clutch, and transmits driving force to the rear wheels.

When the speed of the front wheels becomes even greater than the rear wheels, the torque limiter mechanism (relief valve) limits the hydraulic pressure that engages the wet-type multi-plate clutch, and transmits only the necessar driving force to the rear wheels as needed by 4WD driving.

![](images/ad5e935b9d75500dcc1a3566c8646ebc56d661589bb57e90090dda4cf74ea8b5.webp)

# Construction of the Rear Differential Assembly

The rear differential assembly consists of the torque control diffrential (TCD) that controls the 4WD mechanism and the rear differential mechanism section.

![](images/4875368b37626453f91c836703fd49da341c6b090fd2563c33ef104cab24c137.webp)  
TCD The TCD consists of the TCD case, the differential clutch assembly, the one-way cam, and the oil pump body ass

![](images/b18ba1a630d810f82c22e9db8f3e29a44bb63dbd6cece83a890d4810bd3e51a7.webp)

# Differential clutch assembly

The diffrential clutch assembly is composed of the clutch guide, clutch disc A/B, the clutch hub, the pressure plate, and also the one-way cam, the pilot clutch assembly, and other parts. The clutch guide gets the front wheel driving force from the propelr shaft, while the clutch hub meshes with the hypoid drive pinion gear, and follows the speed of the rear wheels.

![](images/b5ef9b4a063bd30bbac6d9c7c9e407601d4ca62d95778a572ef48fce0254b27d.webp)

# Construction of the one-way cam

The one-way cam consists of the base cam that spins with the clutch guide via the pilot clutch, the apply cam that meshes with the clutch hub, and the steel balls that are sandwiched by the two cams. The base cam rotates at front wheel speed and the apply cam rotates at rear wheel speed.

When speed diference develops, the steel ball move along the grooves in the base cam, and by the shape of the grooves, pushes the apply cam outwards.

![](images/0a2f36882082d893d471ce5f831cd047efde39101ab0a9c01cc3dbe318d9993d.webp)

# Construction of the Rear Differential Assembly (cont'd)

The pump body assembly consists of the front oil pump, the rear oil pump, and the rear oil pump cover, al with a built-in hydraulic circuit. The front oil pump is driven by the pressure plate component.

e rear oil pump is driven by the hypoid drive pinion gear.

The front and rear are both trochoidal pumps. By design, the rear oil pump capacity is set 2.5 % higher than the front oil pump capacity, this i to compensate for the speed diffrence caused by wear in the front tires, as wellas for tight corner braking.

![](images/6b22f516694dc75541ae863692f5f868a67723be8ed1beaed1194317a6938e93.webp)

# Differential carrier

This is composed of the hypoid drive pinion gear, the hypoid ring gear, the differential housing, and other parts.

![](images/043947cb9dcbdbca286c301a1af2f0cb4b1ed9b14ca4aa7564c4c151cb92eff0.webp)  
HONDA

# During 2WD driving: DPS (dual pump system) not in operation

The front wheel driving force from the propeller shaft is transmitted to the clutch guide and the clutch plate. When DPS is not operating, the rear whees follw the front wheels. From the rear driveshafts, the rear wheel operation i input to the differential, the hypoid ring gear, the drive pinion gear, the clutch hub, the clutch disc, and power is not transmitted to the rear wheels.

# During 4WD driving: DPS operation

The front wheel driving force from the propeller shaftis transmitted to the clutch guide and the clutch plate. When the one-way cam operates, the clutch plate and the clutch disc become connected, and from the clutch hub, the driving force is transmitted to the drive pinion gear, the ring gear, the diferential, the rear driveshafts, and to the rear wheels.

![](images/02fd4f34d4a453485c8cc2ee6ca913a63772f7f0873c4623c692e711cc163732.webp)

# Construction of the hydraulic circuit

Built inside the oil pump assembly, the hydraulic circuit provides clutch assembly lubrication together with 4WD control. The hydrauli circuit consists of the front and rear il pumps, the front valve and five check valves for hydraulic route switching, the choke section which is the hydraulic path to the clutch piston compartment, and the two orifices that controls the hydraulic pressure in the piston compartment.

The hydraulic circuit is equipped with a system protection function with a wax-pelt-style thermal switch and relief valve.

![](images/aca2a61ff979dc84e3e91ec374704827672fe330fa73fcef9ee426afc94ea187.webp)

![](images/ec97d2ba4581474d570398e36e065e4cdb47a9701c73fa90b5be48c2d140ed64.webp)

# Operation of the hydraulic pressure circuit

1. Forward starting and acceleration (4WD).

-1.When the front wheel speed exceeds that of the rear wheel speed during forward starting and acceleration, and driving on slippery roads, the front oil pump speed exceeds that of the rear oil pump, thus producing hydraulic pressure.   
-2.The oil drawn in by the front oil pump from the oil strainer, passes through check valve B, and is drawn in or discharged.   
-. Oil discharged from the front oil pump is drawn in by the rear oil pump. However, when the drawing capacity of the rear oil pump is exceeded, the excess oil passes check valve E, is pumped to the piston compartment, pushes the clutch piston to connect it to the clutch assembly, and transmits driving force to the rear wheels.   
4.Oil in the piston compartment is adjusted by the two orifices. Oil that passes through the orifices lubricates and cools the clutch assembly interior and the hypoid pinion gear shaft.

![](images/93a6d0f0272d0eb07b9ba07e7b3ccc1014abed77866373795461f508018f80b8.webp)

2. Forward driving at constant speed (2WD).

-1. When driving forward at a constant speed, the rotation speeds of the front and rear wheels are equal, thus there is no speed difference between the front and rear oil pumps.

-2. Oil discharged from the front oil pump is drawn in by the rear oil pump, and the oil discharged from the rear oil pump is again drawn in by the front oil pump. The oil circulates only between these two oil pumps. Since hydraulic pressure does not develop in the piston compartment, the clutch assembly is not connected, and rear wheel drive is not engaged.

![](images/76cbca2750cf32077a7b9b9a53493f24d1d2b2adc6677c74cada69bb09bb11e6.webp)

3. Forward deceleration (2WD).

-1. During forward deceleration, the rear wheel speeds exceeds the front wheel speed because of braking characteristics, and the rear oil pump speed exceeds the front oil pump speed.   
-2.The oil drawn in by the rear oil pump from the oil strainer, passes through check valve A, and is drawn in or discharged.   
3.Oil discharged from the rear oil pump i again drawn in by the rear oil pump, and is circulated. Because of this, the piston compartment does not produce hydraulic pressure, so that the clutch assembly is not connected, and rear wheel drive is not engaged.

![](images/32b3e1e199c32e037e9c360d23be5d4989e1b5b1bbc456e52b0b0010f64ad951.webp)

4. Reverse starting and deceleration (4WD).

1. When the front wheel speed exceeds that of the rear wheelspeed during reversestarting and acceleration, or when driving on slippery roads, the front oil pump speed exceeds that of the rear oil pump, thus producing hydraulic pressure.   
-2.During reverse driving, the oil pumps rotate in reverse. However, the oil drawn in by the front pump from the oil strainer passes check valve A and the rear oil pump, and then is drawn in and discharged by the front oil pump.   
il ischared by the front i pump ecee he drawingcaacity of the earil pump, passes trough check vave F, travels to the piston compartment, and is pressure-regulated in the two orifices.   
4.Hydraulic pressure pushes the clutch piston to connect it with the clutch assembly interior, and via the propeller shaft, transmits driving force from the transmission to the rear wheels.

![](images/ec99e132290271e7170127ec6510479b6b502abec8cbf672bfab2bbe748b96ae.webp)

# Operation of the hydraulic pressure circuit (cont'd)

5. Reverse driving at constant speed (2WD).

-When reverse driving is at a constant speed, the front and rear wheel speeds are equal, so that no speed diference exists between the front and rear oil pumps.   
-When reverse driving, theil pumps rotate i reverse.However, the il dschared from the front il pump i drawn inby the rear oil pump. Likewise, the oil discharged by the rear oil pump is again drawn in by the front oil pump, and is circulated.   
.The excess oil coming from the diffeence i capacity of the front and rearil pumps, although in smalamounts, passes through check valve E and goes to the piston compartment. However, the hydraulic pressure is low so that the clutch piston is not moved, and rear wheel drive is not engaged.

![](images/ae6139f84541abf707834af88d0ee0bf4eff6ce356f19926d231e0fc6b0c2c8d.webp)

6. Reverse deceleration (4WD).

-.During reverse deceleration, the rea whee speed exceeds the front wheel speed because of braking characteristics, thus causing the rear oil pump speed to exceed the front oil pump speed.   
-2.During reverse driving, the il pump rotates i reverse, but the rearoil pump draws i oil from the oil strainer.The oil pump passes through check valves B and C, and is drawn in by the rear oil pump.   
.Excess oil from the il discharged from the rearoil pump excees the drawing capacit in the front oil pump, passes through check valve E, travels to the piston compartment, and is pressure-regulated at the two orifices.   
4.Hydraulic pressure presses the clutch piston to connect with the clutch assembly interior, and transmits driving force from the transmission to the rear wheels via the propeller shaft.

![](images/93610026103293c21de8b04baeb183c888e73d24917ed11a847e0c0e8256f4ed.webp)

# Emergency hydraulic pressure circuit operation

7. Thermal switch operation.

-1. During 4WD driving, adjusted oil acts on the relief valve and the clutch piston. -2. When the differential oil becomes abnormally hot, the thermal switch pushes the check valve, and the hydraulic pressure in the clutch piston is released, so that 4WD is disabled to protect the system.

![](images/bb17b684c2f3c0ce3ad290be85304daec6ab2f8ec8644f468529bee06eb98ad8.webp)

8. When the relief valve is in operation.

-1. During 4WD, adjusted oil acts on the relief valve and the clutch piston. When hydraulic pressure exceeds the spring tension at the release spring, the check valve opens, the oil pressure in clutch piston is maintained, and excessive torque input to the rear wheel drive system is prevented.

![](images/7befa9b712347cde3f2038df3e2660c76a67bc4fdc6645d697278437bb9583ba.webp)

# Starting and accelerating in forward gears (4WD mode)

NOTE: Do not test repeatedly, or the differential fluid will overheat.

NOTE: Do not test repeatedly, or the differential fluid will overheat.

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 2. Make a mark (A) on either No. 1 or No. 2 propeller shaft (B).

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 2. Make a mark (A) on either No. 1 or No. 2 propeller shaft (B).

![](images/bd22120ea181151dbb60b0a9c147c33b209253affeaac5a0196709fb2d7010de.webp)

![](images/d796287ccbb3079d6a28a56ac5a890d6a037afc0df64caf7aaeebaed89b6a4e5.webp)

3. Start the engine, and let it idle until the radiator fan comes on at least twice.

3. Start the engine, and let it idle until the radiator fan comes on at least twice.

4. With the engine at idle, shift to 1.

5. Firmly apply the parking brake to lock the rear wheels, and watch the rotation of the propeller shaft. If it takes more than 10 seconds to rotate one time, the 4WD system is normal. If it takes less than 10 seconds to rotate one time, there is a problem in the 4WD system. Check the differential fluid first. If the differential fluid is normal, replace the torque control differential (TCD) case kit (front pump portion).

4. With the engine at idle, shift to R.

5. Firmly apply the parking brake to lock the rear wheels, and record the time it takes the propeller shaft to rotate 10 times. If the recorded time is more than 10 seconds, the 4WD system is normal. If the recorded time is less than 10 seconds, there is a problem in the 4WD system. Check the differential fluid first. If the differential fluid is normal, replace the torque control differential (TCD) case kit. \*

# Decelerating in forward gears (2WD mode)

NOTE: The Accord Crosstour/Crosstour V6 has no rear jacking bracket. Do not use the rear differential assembly, the rear subframe, or rear suspension components as jacking points. Use the following procedure to avoid damaging the vehicle.

1. Place the block on the right front wheel.

2. Position the floor jack under the vehicle's left front support point (A). Center the jack lift platform (B) on the support point, and jack up the vehicle high enough to fit a safety stand (C) under the vehicle's rear support point (D).

![](images/0194920f2d33785d3b62761c60b323974b24cfddbd906ac07abec8840e2b4a3b.webp)

3. Carefully lower the jack until the rear support point contacts the safety stand, then remove the jack.

# 4. Block the left front wheel.

5. Hold the left rear tire, and turn it counterclockwise continuously for more than one rotation.

If the rotation of the wheel does not gradualy feel heavy while rotating, the 2WD system when decelerating in a forward gear is normal. If the rotation of the wheel gradually feels heavy while rotating, there is a problem in the system. Check the differential fluid. If the fluid is normal, replace the torque control differential (TCD) case kit.

![](images/009ddb3a82715790d728809ec164537ec3889c29643bfe2684ec2af92023bfe7.webp)

# Decelerating in reverse gears (4WD mode)

NOTE: The Accord Crosstour/Crosstour V6 has no rear jacking bracket. Do not use the rear differential assembly, the rear subframe, or rear suspension components as jacking points. Use the following procedure to avoid damaging the vehicle.

1. Place the block on the right front wheel.

2. Position the floor jack under the vehicle's left front support point (A). Center the jack lift platform (B) on the support point, and jack up the vehicle high enough to fit a safety stand (C) under the vehicle's rear support point (D).

![](images/52e143494a5401b1f3c6ce3b0820a55df9dbaa27fe261444c4dcc0274b511a11.webp)

3. Carefully lower the jack until the rear support point contacts the safety stand, then remove the jack.

4. Block the left front wheel.

5. Hold the left rear tire, and turn it clockwise continuously for more than one rotation.

If the wheel does not rotate, the 4WD system when decelerating in reverse gear is normal. If the wheel rotates, there is a problem in the system. Check the differential fluid. If the fluid is normal, replace the torque control differential (TCD) case kit.

![](images/8809583fcc11eed415def30730ef85f353148a18f6029ae422af5ea122329a59.webp)

# Symptom Troubleshooting Index

Most problems in the unit can be diagnosed by identifying noises from the gears or bearings.   
Be careful during diagnosis not to confuse differential noises with those from other drivetrain components.

# Rear Differential Fluid Inspection and Replacement

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 2. Use solvent and a brush to wash any oil and dirt off the oil filler plug, and dry them with compressed air. 3. Remove the oil filler plug (A) and the sealing washer (B), then check the condition of the rear differential fluid, if the fluid is dirty or burnt, replace it.

![](images/42f859a6ac4e94b43ebd4cd79e524cd2ee5a1304071418a98ea03ccd213cf7a0.webp)

4. Make sure the rear differential fluid is at the proper level (C). If the level is below the proper level, check for rear differential fluid leaks at the differential. If a problem is found, fix it before filling the differential with fluid.

5. The fluid level must reach up to the bottom of the oil filler plug hole. If necessary, add the rear differential fluid until it runs out, then reinstall the oil filler plug with a new sealing washer.

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 2. Remove the oil filler plug (A) and the sealing washer (B).

![](images/d720022df9eb91c88e69c1eb54950bae81ee24097c4d4e41a72a5949a9d0d291.webp)

3. Remove the drain plug (A) and the sealing washer (B), then drain the rear differential fluid.

![](images/3e06460bf994ca416e0797a767d5673e3989092baca7a554e665a38fc1858eaa.webp)

4. Clean the drain plug, then reinstall it with a new sealing washer.

5. Refill the differential with rear differential fluid to the proper level.

NOTE: If you disassemble the differential, check the rear differential fluid level again after the 4WD system check is finished. Add fluid if necessary.

Fluid Capacity: 1.2 L(1.3 US qt) at fluid change 1.4 L (1.5 US qt) at overhaul

Recommended fluid: Honda Dual Pump Fluid II

6. Reinstall the oil filler plug with a new sealing washer.

7. If the Maintenance Minder required to replace the rear differential fluid, reset the Maintenance Minder, and this procedure is complete. If the Maintenance Minder did not require to replace the rear differential fluid, go to step 9.

8. Lower the vehicle.

9. With the ignition switch in LOCK (0), then connect the HDS to the DLC (A) located under the driver's side of the dashboard.

![](images/dafb0e56401a0c4dde6928324914cbc5c36f88fdc8f411ffa1ef854b689e71ec.webp)

10. Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il).

11. Make sure the HDS communicates with the vehicle and the PCM. If it does not communicate, troubleshoot the DLC circuit (see page 11-430).   
12. Select GAUGES in the BODY ELECTRICAL with the HDS.   
13. Select ADJUSTMENT in the GAUGES with the HDS.   
14. Select MAINTENANCE MINDER in the ADJUSTMENT with the HDS.   
15. Select MAINTENANCE SUB ITEM 6 RESET with the HDS, and reset the rear differential fluid life.

# Rear Differential Removal

2. Drain the rear differential fluid (see page 15-22).   
3. Remove the rear wheels.   
4. Remove the muffler (see page 9-12).   
5. Remove the lower arm A mounting bolts (A) and the   
lower arm B mounting bolts (B).

# Differential Housing Assembly Removal and Installation

1. Remove the rear differential mounting stiffener and rear differential mounting bracket B (see page 15-37). 2. Remove the nine mounting bolts in a crisscross pattern in several steps, then remove the differential housing assembly (A), the two dowel pins (B) (if equipped), and the oil seals (C).

![](images/0ee6cdf42e19071f3404799b08d36dca6d26454c1e6ee23cccf0aa7a514d800f.webp)

# Differential Housing Assembly Removal and Installation (cont'd)

3. Remove the dirt and oil from the sealing surfaces. Apply liquid gasket (P/N 08717-0004, 08718-0001, 08718-0003, 08718-0004, or 08718-0009) evenly to the sealing surface. Install the component within 5 minutes of applying the liquid gasket. Make sure you seal the entire circumference of the bolt holes to prevent fluid leakage.

# NOTE:

If you apply liquid gasket P/N 08718-0012, the component must be installed within 4 minutes. If too much time has passed after applying the liquid gasket, remove the old liquid gasket and residue, then reapply the new liquid gasket. Allow it to cure at least 30 minutes after assembly before filling the differential with the recommended fluid.

![](images/0ad58f45804b110899925247702bd6c0fcca504955e7a1f8c9f3cd492896c2c2.webp)

![](images/aabb7ddbee71f5dbf2e056743e137dd6a5845197b2941b4931cdaaf7505c4cb0.webp)

5. Install the new oil seals (D) (see step 2 on page 15-27). 6. Reinstall rear differential mounting brackets B and the rear differential mounting stiffener (see page 15-37).

32Nm (3.3 kgfm 24b-ft) Replace.

![](images/82e4a17e910d9e1fffd6046fb9c1e9dd50f64683d66049b4433d4317a253a20f.webp)

10. Loosely install the new lower arm A mounting bolts (A) and the new lower arm B mounting bolts (B).

B   
12 × 1.25mm   
64 Nm (6.5 kgf.m, 47 lbf.ft) Replace.   
11. Place a floor jack under the lower arm, and raise the suspension to load it with the vehicle's weight.   
12. Tighten the lower arm A mounting bolts and the lower arm B mounting bolts to the specified torque.   
13. Install the muffler (see page 9-12).   
14. Clean the mating surfaces between the brake disc/drum and the inside of the wheel, then install the rear wheels.   
15. Refill the rear differential with the recommended fluid (see page 15-22).   
16. Check the wheel alignment, and adjust it if necessary (see page 18-5).   
17. Test-drive the vehicle.

# Front Driveshaft Removal

1. Check the inboard boot (A) and the outboard boot (B) on the driveshaft (C) for cracks, damage, leaking grease, and loose boot bands (D). If any damage is found, replace the boot and the boot bands.

![](images/0191470dc3d4facba65d708659f85cb0d7db41c0180a9714a9b56756b80c6833.webp)

2. Check the driveshaft for cracks and damage. If any damage is found, replace the driveshaft.   
3. Check the inboard joint (E) and the outboard joint (F) for cracks and damage. If any damage is found, replace the inboard joint or the outboard joint as an assembly.   
4. Hold the inboard joint and turn the wheel by hand, then make sure the joint is not excessively loose. If necessary, replace the inboard joint or the outboard joint as an assembly.

# Special Tools Required

Ball Joint Thread Protector, 14 mm 07AAE-SJAA100   
• Ball Joint Remover, 32 mm 07MAC-SL0A102

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12).

2. Remove the front wheel.

3. Pry up the stake (A) on the spindle nut (B), then remove the nut.

![](images/f49bf1326aba03346c53e00e11f84b35a16d537287d91dff55fb18b2cdf0637d.webp)

4. Drain the transmission fluid, then reinstall the drain plug with a new sealing washer (see page 14-192).

5. Hold the stabilizer link joint pin (A) using a hex wrench (B), and remove the flange nut (C). Separate the front stabilizer link (D) from the lower arm.

![](images/ed922ad6a58f847281a6e27345f548788fb32fefd4961fb2c103933605aae515.webp)

6. Remove the damper pinch bolt (A) and the damper fork mounting nut (B) while holding the mounting bolt (C), then remove the damper fork (D) from the damper and the lower arm.

![](images/22786f319c848169faf6fdd03e477538869ed182c3e649fa3c69e930ab43aa89.webp)

7. Remove the cotter pin (A) from the knuckle ball joint, then remove the castle nut (B). Separate the ball joint from the lower arm (C) using the 32 mm ball joint remover (D) and the 14 mm ball joint thread protector (E) (see page 18-11).

# NOTE:

Be careful not to damage the ball joint boot when installing the remover.   
Do not force or hammer on the lower arm, or pry between the lower arm and the knuckle. You could damage the ball joint.

![](images/f78127c0802fecf457220d3691ee67c11f81d301db576c360ca318f75d8ca04c.webp)

8. Pull the knuckle outward, and separate the outboard joint from the front hub using a soft face hammer.

![](images/1575a42b35f9e5d2de819ab8c2cbcadbd10a4135c875cbdb76643fa24f8b226e.webp)

9. Remove exhaust pipe A. 2WD model (see page 9-11) 4WD model (see page 9-12)

# Front Driveshaft Removal (cont'd)

10. Left driveshaft: Pry the inboard joint (A) from the differential using a pry bar. Remove the driveshaft as an assembly.

# NOTE:

Do not pull on the driveshaft (B), or the inboard joint may come apart. Pull the inboard joint straight out to avoid damaging the oil seal. Be careful not to damage the oil seal or the end of the inboard joint with the pry bar.

![](images/7a6ec328dfd7a165f6fa45bceae93a1792c5e7f55af18a892b21af5f239a4b6d.webp)

11. Right driveshaft: Drive the inboard joint (A) off of the intermediate shaft using a drift punch and a hammer. Remove the driveshaft as an assembly.

NOTE: Do not pull on the driveshaft (B), or the inboard joint may come apart.

![](images/237ddede5405557644b25af980bb8ad5531f78e4c65f81d290efe29388e3cf56.webp)

12. Remove the set ring (A) from the left driveshaft inboard joint.

![](images/9afdf727768d76b2354894e7575f134dcbc3c04d83fb7c1d4cc7ab50527c1200.webp)

13. Remove the set ring (A) from the intermediate shaft.

![](images/05d01f099a505773fadd703cc14ecdb2538b9a3b3a40c36826ba44893fa0b0fb.webp)

# Front Driveshaft Disassembly

Threaded Adapter, 26 x 1.5 mm 07XAC-001030A Slide Hammer 5/8"-18 UNF, commercially available Bearing Puller, commercially available Boot Band Pliers, commercially available

# Inboard Joint Side

1. Remove the boot bands. Be careful not to damage the boot.

If the boot band is a welded type (A), cut the boot band.   
If the boot band is a double loop type (B), Iift up the band end (C), and push it into the clip (D).   
If the boot band is a low profile type (E), pinch the boot band using commercially available boot band pliers (F).

# Welded type

![](images/dbd7da784b984ed9931424c8fea4e6816725fea7fbbd8214e2ec4c9e625ef00b.webp)

# Double loop type

![](images/84b2de85b23fd4ed2047eac57ab4babcb14da0887fe72528b7663bb2327139a5.webp)

Low profile type

![](images/11fcb54d885a156efa967aa34c1a3cf325f48392b455dab8a3ab2fd05d0c1147.webp)

2. Make marks (A) on each roller (B) and the inboard joint (C) to identify the locations of the rollers to the grooves in the inboard joint.

NOTE: Do not engrave or scribe any marks on the rolling surface.

![](images/838dfe21b35a32f6f24d8332cca1a6a2dcacbb278319d1cb5df053863df19514.webp)

3. Remove the inboard joint on a clean shop towel (D). Be careful not to drop the rollers when separating them from the inboard joint.

# Front Driveshaft Disassembly (cont'd)

4. Make marks (A) on the spider (B) that match the marks on the rollers, then remove the rollers.

NOTE: Do not engrave or scribe any marks on the rolling surface.

![](images/ef8d6733a748a55bb5b977444397ee75be10eb48c545166b1c1bba4e0fb2d761.webp)

5. Remove the circlip (C).

6. Make marks (D) on the spider and the driveshaft (E) to identify the position of the spider on the shaft.

7. Remove the spider.

NOTE: If necessary, use a commercially available bearing puller while being careful not to damage the spider.

8. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the inboard boot.

![](images/56f4fdd9d9478dac1667d66947f5056990c9c6a5e47d68782dab97c70258cdbf.webp)

9. Remove the inboard boot. Be careful not to damage the boot.

10. Remove the vinyl tape.

# Outboard Joint Side

1. Remove the ear clamp bands (A). Lift up the three tabs (B) using a flat-tipped screwdriver, then release the band. Be careful not to damage the boot.

![](images/c76a40c5e1df8df9f6be4a4e347e7f6b4f827b6199899dcc35de42489773fc50.webp)

2. Slide the outboard boot (A) partially toward the inboard joint side. Be careful not to damage the boot.

![](images/5062ebeef220ebf8db2c9848b1a23b5f777314454311f03e293e10a55dab40a3.webp)

3. Wipe off the grease to expose the driveshaft and the outboard joint inner race.   
4. Make a mark (A) on the driveshaft (B) at the same level as the outboard joint end (C).

![](images/006b45a2eb7737f792fe648b97c8879f41b0245ac61afe078e9138c06bf14a39.webp)

5. Securely clamp the driveshaft in a bench vise with a shop towel wrapped around the driveshaft. 6. Remove the outboard joint (A) using the 26 x 1.5 mm threaded adapter (B) and a commercially available 5/8"-18 UNF slide hammer (C).

![](images/c649e5cd7ed42d7c610694b74941540d8d920f580b56352b55d450939b282343.webp)

7. Remove the driveshaft from the bench vise.

8. Remove the stop ring (A) from the driveshaft.

![](images/43367f4e785ee4a2b36f09a6201a9b5b3b6a0d671e6105e4fb106edb6e336e46.webp)

9. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the outboard boot.

![](images/90d8df6e5c6568e854f09210876537082c27953d17d902b4105376dab1735a5d.webp)

10. Remove the outboard boot. Be careful not to damage the boot.

11. Remove the vinyl tape.

# Front Driveshaft Reassembly

![](images/ef5d6b4b089e45d3091771848d0720005e35cba6f6629803afaed6abdf473b57.webp)

# Special Tools Required

•Boot Band Tool KD-3191 or equivalent, commercially available •Boot Band Clamp Tool Kent-Moore J-35910 or equivalent, commercially available •Boot Band Pliers, commercially available

NOTE: Refer to the Exploded View, as needed, during this procedure.

# Inboard Joint Side

1. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the inboard boot.

![](images/f6754a02b16fc5732cfbf5c6bc19955ec643280609889faa5e024bcdcf848ac9.webp)

2. Install the inboard boot onto the driveshaft, then remove the vinyl tape. Be careful not to damage the inboard boot.

3. Install the spider (A) onto the driveshaft by aligning the marks (B) you made on the spider and the end of the driveshaft.

![](images/930fb2e9c1d607967628509bafbf8ff01ffd59fbc24eb5d2936dfd4c33fe7f6d.webp)

4. Install a new circlip (C) into the driveshaft groove. Always rotate the circlip in its groove to make sure it is fully seated.

5. Fit the rollers (A) onto the spider (B) as shown, and note these items: •Reinstall the rollers in their original positions on the spider by aligning the marks (C) you made. Hold the driveshaft pointed up to prevent the rollers from falling off.

![](images/756baeb602985010801be2f60897a9d65d3daaa3e9701d4f6e163f213acfaa51.webp)

# Front Driveshaft Reassembly (cont'd)

6. Pack the inboard joint with the joint grease included in the new inboard boot set.

Grease quantity Inboard joint: 110— 120 g (3.88—4.23 oz)

![](images/325e25aabefbefb7396b6c82f3300eca33c14ed4ff4316dfcfb7e0d109ca1d87.webp)

7. Fit the inboard joint onto the driveshaft, and note these items:

Reinstall the inboard joint onto the driveshaft by aligning the marks (A) you made on the inboard joint and the rollers. Hold the driveshaft so the inboard joint is pointing up to prevent it from falling off.

![](images/4fbce86d907d3e73379d826f51c10c491a9292f1b3e5ee7967fce5759ff23d6a.webp)

8. Fit the boot ends (A) onto the driveshaft (B) and the inboard joint (C).

![](images/f54fd9a775a861e5a99aad54a5e4834845dbe5538f828a551033d5d42f8c581f.webp)

9. Adjust the length (A) of the driveshafts in the figure as shown, then adjust the boots to halfway between full compression and full extension. Bleed excess air from the boots by inserting a flat-tipped screwdriver between the boot and the joint.

Left driveshaft: 599—604 mm (23.58—23.78 in)

А

![](images/a27e164fbab8625c57e87233ddde2e37cee9c094cc4cf8128b71078170b56be8.webp)  
Right driveshaft: 557 —562 mm (21.93—22.13 in)

10. Install new boot bands.

For the double loop type, go to step 11.   
For the low profile type, go to step 20.

11. Fit the boot ends onto the driveshaft and the inboard joint, then install a new double loop band (A) onto the boot (B).

NOTE: Pass the end of the double loop band through the clip (C) twice in the direction of the forward rotation of the driveshaft.

![](images/d54dd8d1acc9e65e8a3d70645e4486d79111ba7cee7196a2d8ea8568a6bac1e6.webp)

12. Pull up the slack in the band by hand.

13. Mark a line (A) on the band 10— 14 mm (0.39—0.55 in) from the clip (B).

![](images/6b0d0aaf9ee62d3274724889dbbac5f0458f0c019bafbecbaf45d97e2ee739e3.webp)

14. Thread the free end of the band through the nose section of the commercially available boot band tool (KD-3191 or equivalent) (A), and into the slot on the winding mandrel (B).

![](images/ae9c7844ff17e3b892a6de3e5b68f5b85a29315df76e6f6bc85761a08b9b4f76.webp)

15. Using a wrench on the winding mandrel of the boot band tool, tighten the band until the marked line (C) on the band meets the edge of the clip.

16. Lift up the boot band tool to bend the free end of the band 90 degrees to the clip. Center-punch the clip, then fold over the remaining tail onto the clip.

![](images/058b64cb2620295ebff8ef85511bbe0ea3deb74652e8b9f75f6dc434a6ce5662.webp)

# Front Driveshaft Reassembly (cont'd)

17. Unwind the boot band tool, and cut off the excess free end of the band to leave a 5— 10 mm (0.20 —0.39 in) tail protruding from the clip.

![](images/42b554361729c27bc6900d909608eb40474e7b33c9cd088da1a3b0060fcb5396.webp)

18. Bend the band end (A) by tapping it down using a hammer.

NOTE:

Make sure the band and the clip do not interfere with anything on the vehicle, and the band does not move.   
Clean any grease remaining on the surrounding surfaces.

![](images/c90b2737b68281a07c9b69b57f95cfe24d97da608a3101e17596143ba805863c.webp)

19. Repeat steps 11 through 18 for the band on the other end of the boot.

20. Fit the boot ends onto the driveshaft and the inboard joint. Install a new low profile band (A) onto the boot (B), then hook the tab () of the band.

![](images/fa3be78b65e1b264ae7300f615cebd4bbb225c64e838bbce97ec9e0d0524ac85.webp)

21. Close the hook portion of the band using commercially available boot band pliers (A), then hook the tabs (B) of the band.

![](images/8da38bef8e7a290953a9669c1e24d1915ba6e4335563264e6fd770e1b0336cfb.webp)

22. Instal the boot band on the other end of the boot, and repeat steps 20 and 21.

# Outboard Joint Side

1. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the outboard boot.

![](images/964b4ae7d9bb8ea218189e539ea9e603fbced115e485fc5445621a517b39ad8e.webp)

2. Install new ear clamp bands (B) and the outboard boot onto the driveshaft, then remove the vinyl tape. Be careful not to damage the outboard boot.

3. Make sure to check the size of a new stop ring.

# NOTICE

To avoid driveshaft and vehicle damage, make sure you install a new stop ring.

Stop ring specifications Overall diameter (A): 29.2 mm (1.150 in) Wire diameter (B): 2.0 mm (0.079 in)

![](images/4d546652c3f2742a201ca624f1b0a1b6d10878b052199404157324f992dc32f1.webp)

4. Install the stop ring (A) into the driveshaft groove (B).

![](images/3107e4225277da5bef235bab03aa441782ea3466f9660e7f08353631bfbf1c7c.webp)

5. Pack about 35 g (1.23 oz) of grease included in the new outboard boot set into the driveshaft hole in the outboard joint.

NOTE: If you are installing a new outboard joint, the grease is already installed.

![](images/30285a8a8317ac2ab27b81bfc60f673ebd48342870ff9c99aa5709caa546fb51.webp)

# Front Driveshaft Reassembly (cont'd)

6. Insert the driveshaft (A) into the outboard joint (B) until the stop ring (C) is close to the joint.

![](images/3c2da42ddcc353f696a5bb6704ea7619a9cd1fb49ecec9e0848b7487ccca71d5.webp)

7. To completely seat the outboard joint, pick up the driveshaft and the joint, and tap or hit the assembly onto a hard surface from a height of about 10 cm (3.9 in).

NOTE: Do not use a hammer, as excessive force may damage the driveshaft. Be careful not to damage the threaded section (A) of the outboard joint.

![](images/0257c73cb0339655847c0b96f37754849b4773812834649beda03ceaa0adf449.webp)

8. Check the alignment of the paint mark (A) you made with the outboard joint end (B).

# NOTICE

To avoid driveshaft and vehicle damage, the shaft must be al the way into the outboard joint to ensure the stop ring is properly seated.

![](images/f96e33b9985ede216612de14f4310262bab117c5ef6c2903f37b04bf98013243.webp)

9. Pack the outboard joint (A) with the remaining joint grease included in the outboard boot set.

Total grease quantity Outboard joint:  140 — 150 g (4.94 —5.29 oz)

![](images/ba6dacec72ab5900a1cc68651d562a23f2d1e02fad25559837e138b6997fe308.webp)

Use the grease included in the outboard boot set.

10. Fit the boot ends (A) onto the driveshaft (B) and the outboard joint (C). Bleed any excess air from the boot by inserting a flat-tipped screwdriver between the boot and the joint.

![](images/2adc24b56394021592543830ff9bd658c0a3d6d718f2bf12f0c68f444257b8e4.webp)  
Right driveshaft: 557—562 mm (21.93—22.13 in)

11. Inspect the length (A) of the driveshafts in the figure as shown, then adjust the boots to halfway between full compression and full extension.

Left driveshaft: 599 —604 mm (23.58—23.78 in)

A

A

12. Close the ear portion (A) of the band using a commercially available boot band clamp tool (Kent-Moore J-35910 or equivalent) (B).

![](images/1a3a6143988a5ab9ae213d21e4dc17bdfdb98980c72b2c9edf3312f35855b76b.webp)

13. Check the clearance between the closed ear portion of the band. If the clearance is not within the standard, close the ear portion of the band tighter.

![](images/603573c75eadd195a0c3218b448daa9567f76aafcee5f4de3008a07d450f5cdc.webp)

14. Repeat steps 12 and 13 for the band on the other end of the boot.

# Front Driveshaft Installation

NOTE: Before starting installation, make sure the mating surfaces of the joint and the splined section are clean.

1. Apply about 5 g (0.18 oz) of moly 60 paste (P/N 08734-0001) to the contact area (A) of the outboard joint and the front wheel bearing.

NOTE: The paste helps prevent noise and vibration.

![](images/8b6642ba131acee397da02aae1ffec691d7bda5aeef4cb67b81bd2c21196fcb0.webp)

2. Install a new set ring (A) into the set ring groove (B) of the left driveshaft inboard joint.

![](images/79b0e98d243fe778bd57e5fd58bca6c98827cea00eaec5055ba8d8976f55543a.webp)

3. Install a new set ring (A) into the set ring groove (B) of the intermediate shaft.

![](images/e7e7941e1721bc6b2aed6602cb1fc895f1eb9681dfeb85c1a7312d96ecfc33ed.webp)

4.Apply 0.5—1.0 g (0.018-0.035oz) of super high temp urea grease (P/N 08798-9002) to the whole splined surface (A) of the right driveshaft. After applying grease, remove the grease from the splined grooves at intervals of 2—3 splines and from the set ring groove (B) so that air can bleed from the intermediate shaft.

![](images/9bcdc70bac3c0ce4fe6e46e14eab5ff8029e8c6076c7cd49d57ccf4cc4df1c4d.webp)

7. Install the outboard joint (A) into the front hub on the knuckle.

![](images/427611bdc04008aaad056b9fd990b5e4a5beef293385498dc8074484151a4e7e.webp)

8. Install exhaust pipe A. 2WD model (see page 9-11) 4WD model (see page 9-12)

5. Clean the areas where the driveshaft contacts the differential thoroughly with solvent, and drythem with compressed air.

NOTE: Do not wash the rubber parts with solvent.

6. Insert the inboard end (A) of the driveshaft into the differential (B) or the intermediate shaft (C) until the set ring (D) locks in the groove (E).

NOTE: Insert the driveshaft horizontally to prevent damaging the oil seal.

![](images/f0b3ed95b5902b54e937d4d2aaec444630c9305cce4b25d4b97cf7449f437c1a.webp)

9. Wipe off any grease contamination from the ball joint tapered section and threads, then install the knuckle (A) onto the lower arm (B). Be careful not to damage the ball joint boot (C). Wipe off the grease before tightening the nut at the ball joint. Torque the castle nut (D) to the lower torque specification, then tighten it only far enough to align the slot with the ball joint pin hole.

# NOTE:

Make sure the ball joint boot is not damaged or cracked. Do not align the nut by loosening it.

![](images/7d6b0684073fac956f14dd156937914fcac7fe94c1cd19200ed473d79a76c11d.webp)

10. Install a new cotter pin (E) into the ball joint pin hole, and bend the cotter pin as shown.

# Front Driveshaft Installation (cont'd)

11. Install the damper fork (A) over the driveshaft and onto the lower arm. Install the damper in the damper fork so the aligning tab (B) is aligned with the slot in the damper fork. Loosely install the damper pinch bolt (C).

![](images/beafdd1c63198569faab5f70512c6c6704f81ec4b395df20072cfd6cb615c79e.webp)

12. Loosely install a new damper fork mounting bolt (D) and a new damper fork mounting nut (E). 13. Connect the front stabilizer link (A) to the lower arm, and loosely install a new flange nut (B). Hold the stabilizer link joint pin (C) using a hex wrench (D), and tighten the flange nut.

![](images/cb0d9d5b3fa9f955aff3a300a6c11a0d873bdcb74f0147ab828aaea9905095a0.webp)

14. Place a floor jack under the lower arm, and raise the suspension to load it with the vehicle's weight. NOTE: Do not put the floor jack under the ball joint.   
15. Tighten the damper pinch bolt and the damper fork mounting nut while holding the damper fork mounting bolt to the specified torque values, then remove the floor jack.   
16. Apply a small amount of engine oil to the seating surface of a new spindle nut (A).   
17. Install the spindle nut, then tighten it. After tightening, use a drift to stake the spindle nut shoulder (B) against the driveshaft.   
18. Clean the mating surfaces between the brake disc and the inside of the wheel, then install the front wheel.   
19. Turn the wheel by hand, and make sure there is no interference between the driveshaft and surrounding parts.   
20. Lower the vehicle.   
21. Refill the transmission with the recommended transmission fluid (see page 14-192).   
22. Check the wheel alignment, and adjust it if necessary (see page 18-5).

![](images/447a447c4115283891f087317f8ea1060b0b70bc32b8b43c5b5dd2a451a74dc1.webp)

23. Test-drive the vehicle.

# Intermediate Shaft Removal

1. Drain the transmission fluid, then reinstall the drain plug with a new sealing washer (see page 14-192).

2. Remove exhaust pipe A. 2WD model (see page 9-11) 4WD model (see page 9-12)

3. Remove the right front driveshaft (see page 16-4).

4. Remove the rear warm up three way catalytic converter (rear WU-TWC) bracket (A).

![](images/1184d0289a2c09f5475e935613b846b5fca5ca1c5ec3f07cf3d388e34a9e96e4.webp)

5. Remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor cover (A).

6. Disconnect the CKP sensor connector (A), and remove the bolt (B) securing the sensor harness clamp bracket (C).

![](images/1c41d1b0bb5a06d35fda4bf883e97c132b7d2301227dda566a89fb2a128ecdcd.webp)

7. Swing the sensor harness (D) out of the way to prevent damaging it.

8. Remove the flange bolt (A) and the two dowel bolts (B).

![](images/1f8c68318c9e3d486bf9843dab815dea052102bc91805909e07a82422181380f.webp)

# Intermediate Shaft Installation

1. Clean the areas where the intermediate shaft contacts the differential thoroughly with solvent, and dry them with compressed air.

NOTE: Do not wash the rubber parts with solvent.

2. Install a new set ring (A) into the set ring groove (B) of the intermediate shaft (C).

![](images/39d1b6484666209d394b0d93afc1ac2570c4562dc71a8bacb318e35fbcda0986.webp)

NOTE: Insert the intermediate shaft carefully to prevent damaging the oil seal (D).

9. Install exhaust pipe A. 2WD model (see page 9-11) 4WD model (see page 9-12)

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12).   
2. Remove the rear wheel.   
3. Pry up the stake (A) on the spindle nut (B), then remove the nut.

NOTE:

Be careful not to damage the wheel speed sensor (B). Pull on the outboard joint. Do not pull on the driveshaft because the joint may come apart.

# Inboard Joint Side

1. Remove the boot bands. Be careful not to damage the boot.

For the ear clamp type (see step 1 on page 16-8).   
For the double loop type (see step 1 on page 16-7).

2. Make marks (A) on each roller (B) and the inboard joint (C) to identify the locations of the rollers to the grooves in the inboard joint.

NOTE: Do not engrave or scribe any marks on the rolling surface.

![](images/bdc8f1bef1527bd6224f26a4fee298a5a87c249d3b48841aaa2e3c4b262f3cee.webp)

4. Remove the circlip (A).

# Outboard Joint Side

![](images/1e47bd50ccbfddd4e6e4f1ac7414243904d4cbca536990460579915436d499b6.webp)

1. Remove the boot bands. Be careful not to damage the boot (see step 1 on page 16-8). 2. Slide the outboard boot (A) partially toward the inboard joint side. Be careful not to damage the boot.

7. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the inboard boot.

. Remove the vinyl tape.

# Rear Driveshaft Reassembly

# Special Tools Required

Boot Band Clamp Tool Kent-Moore J-35910 or equivalent, commercially available

NOTE: Refer to the Exploded View, as needed, during this procedure.

# Inboard Joint Side

1. Wrap the splines on the driveshaft with vinyl tape (A) to prevent damaging the inboard boot.

![](images/f65b1f3a75c0a7f0eaf0ff0c67b717bbd935ad68afc87b09daab02ea14f1149c.webp)

2. Install new ear clamp bands (B) and the inboard boot onto the driveshaft, then remove the vinyl tape. Be careful not to damage the inboard boot. 3. Install the spider (A) onto the driveshaft by aligning the marks (B) you made on the spider and the end of the driveshaft.

![](images/2d8f80f5866aa3305b5d691f28f4a2e9e3c6e2d998f5813adc40fa71573bd70c.webp)

4. Install a new circlip (C) into the driveshaft groove. Always rotate the circlip in its groove to make sure it is fully seated.

5. Pack the inboard joint with the joint grease included in the new inboard boot set.

Grease quantity Inboard joint:  96— 124 g (3.39—4.37 oz)

![](images/3ede7a126e8f40c88370d358b6d02d2773f4e64fc8ae81d5f2b3b6130b563aef.webp)

Reinstall the inboard joint onto the driveshaft by aligning the marks (A) you made on the inboard joint and the rollers. Hold the driveshaft so the inboard joint is pointing up to prevent it from falling off.

8. Adjust the length (A) of the driveshafts in the figure as shown, then adjust the boots to halfway between full compression and full extension. Bleed excess air from the boots by inserting a flat-tipped screwdriver between the boot and the joint.

Left driveshaft: 710—715 mm (27.95—28.15 in)   
Right driveshaft: 734— 739 mm (28.90 —29.09 in)

![](images/46ef849b949b42f7398e673a42189bc7782c76160f1c7a7cf96327e766d7053a.webp)

10. Fit the boot ends onto the driveshaft and the inboard joint. Close the ear portion (A) of the band using a commercially available boot band clamp tool (Kent-Moore J-35910 or equivalent) (B).

![](images/464ceda51e0c9b39c4d33b393c066511145acd31b98f6e6bc08c484f6705287d.webp)

# Outboard Joint Side

# NOTICE

To avoid driveshaft and vehicle damage, make sure you install a new stop ring.

Stop ring specifications Overall diameter (A): 20.2 mm (0.795 in) Wire diameter (B): 1.44 mm (0.0567 in)

![](images/d7cc8b9b5ffdd8ff0e86d7550b75cc5ecde05b08890f8a419a0fadb0ff1e21b4.webp)

# Rear Driveshaft Reassembly (cont'd)

6. Insert the driveshaft (A) into the outboard joint (B) until the stop ring (C) is closed to the joint.

7. To completely seat the outboard joint, pick up the driveshaft and the joint, and tap or hit the assembly onto a hard surface from a height of about 10 cm (3.9 in).

NOTE: Do not use a hammer, as excessive force may damage the driveshaft. Be careful not to damage the threaded section (A) of the outboard joint.

![](images/9194fe3c4572cff4ef6eaf61a1d9ae2ca20e831a52c292e079550cceacc8fc7d.webp)

To avoid driveshaft and vehicle damage, the shaft must be all the way into the outboard joint to ensure the stop ring is properly seated.

![](images/e34d685cd1a1a8120f5b2ae10691930c4f917b4ab768a29d481950f334695c5c.webp)

9. Pack the outboard joint (A) with the remaining joint grease included in the outboard boot set.

![](images/475a2d05d736e313e9d7f74702f62986e6abaff35231b55fed55fbe93ade65df.webp)

10. Fit the boot ends (A) onto the driveshaft (B) and the outboard joint (C). Bleed any excess air from the boot by inserting a flat-tipped screwdriver between the boot and the joint.

11. Inspect the length (A) of the driveshafts in the figure as shown, then adjust the boots to halfway between full compression and full extension.

Left driveshaft: 710—715 mm (27.95—28.15 in)   
Right driveshaft: 734— 739 mm (28.90 — 29.09 in)

12. Close the ear portion (A) of the band using a commercially available boot band clamp tool (Kent-Moore J-35910 or equivalent) (B).

![](images/27cceeea1e0c2e8a6f1acef4fdb0c99e906dd7715289f6852ff4109cabbb122b.webp)

13. Check the clearance between the closed ear portion of the band. If the clearance is not within the standard, close the ear portion of the band tighter.

![](images/6bc044233b502bba59bc73bae4bd5a7128a1b71fd34bf4d96f7f22fd6f446e05.webp)  
3.5 mm (0.138 in) max.

14. Repeat steps 12 and 13 for the band on the other end of the boot.

# Rear Driveshaft Installation

NOTE: Before starting installation, make sure the mating surfaces of the joint and the splined section are clean.

1. Install a new set ring (A) into the set ring groove (B) of the rear driveshaft inboard joint.

![](images/c8d6b7d69c479357657ef8e372d05a02264e885a1aef1f98817fb7e509760a3e.webp)

2. Install the outboard joint (A) into the rear hub (B). NOTE: Be careful not to damage the wheel speed sensor (C).

![](images/46537733222b9154d97f94eef4f2670bff637661b323014cfcba518f5739b3a5.webp)

3. Clean the areas where the driveshaft contacts the differential thoroughly with solvent, and dry them with compressed air.

NOTE: Do not wash the rubber parts with solvent.

4. Insert the inboard end (A) of the driveshaft into the differential (B) until the set ring (C) locks in the groove (D).

NOTE: Insert the driveshaft horizontally to prevent damaging the oil seal.

![](images/c03eb2e8760b82ac5ec290e583b727c0b0541e09fd116ad682fa30fd65945040.webp)

5. Install the rear differential (see page 15-39).

6. Apply a small amount of engine oil to the seating surface of a new spindle nut (A).

![](images/5278bdfa1208b86973da9c96dce386e6e996a75ed0c0729ae0ae37b8f569832c.webp)

7.Install the spindle nut, then tighten it. After tightening, use a drift to stake the spindle nut shoulder (B) against the driveshaft.   
8. Clean the mating surfaces between the brake disc/drum and the inside of the wheel, then install the rear wheel.   
9. Turn the wheel by hand, and make sure there is no interference between the driveshaft and surrounding parts.   
10. Refill the rear differential with the recommended fluid (see page 15-22).   
11. Lower the vehicle.   
12. Check the wheel alignment, and adjust it if necessary (see page 18-5).

13. Test-drive the vehicle.

# Propeller Shaft Inspection

1. Move the shift lever to N. 2. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 3. Check the center support bearing (A) for excessive play or noise. If the center support has excessive play or noise, replace the propeller shaft assembly.

![](images/deb10ae65575844c3f7daec1ba9b2af3ff22953e4e39d7aa284844926f621551.webp)

4.Check the rubber portion (B) of the center support bearing for damage and deterioration. If the rubber portion is damaged or deteriorated, replace the propeller shaft assembly. 5. Check the universal joints for excessive play or noise. If the universal joints have excessive play or noise, replace the propeller shaft assembly.

# Propeller Shaft Inspection (cont'd) Propeller Shaft Removal

1. Move the shift lever to N.

2. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12). 3. Install a dial indicator with its needle on the center of the No. 1 propeller shaft or the No. 2 propeller shaft. 4. Turn the other propeller shaft slowly and check the runout. Repeat this procedure for the other propeller shaft.

![](images/b6a8df46a7e9ff8dff685508b5ca74c2539fcc917c9e78b7d05d16cd2e535e14.webp)  
No. 1 Propeller Shaft Runout Service Limit: 1.5 mm (0.059 in)

![](images/72fccba388eef4fb52e6952e59426809395b3036e6acf237f276c0b6c4a7de8a.webp)  
No. 2 Propeller Shaft Runout Service Limit: 1.5 mm (0.059 in)

5. If the runout on either propeller shaft exceeds the service limit, replace the propeller shaft assembly.

1. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12).

2. Remove the propeller shaft protector (A).

![](images/ee520106cae2831d21debe13af3d46e309f57601ffa85100d6a1a3cb51b9968e.webp)

3. Make reference mark (A) across the No. 1 propeller shaft (B) and the transfer companion flange ().

![](images/1e3ffe45120fb1ceddcb3d47210168b145c67287385c9ed09dd62f1a281be054.webp)

4. Remove the No. 1 propeller shaft flange bolts (D).

5. Remove the center support bearing mounting bolts (A).

![](images/614de7e24e1b76cc57e6ac27d14b0d69b0cbe5347d3ad10cd0d5aaeee58860b0.webp)

6. Make reference mark (A) across the No. 2 propeller shaft (B) and the rear differential companion flange (C).

![](images/f48490868499d4cc3bd758ad29acaa5ca2af04e66770f41cb2b94824fafd73b8.webp)

7. Remove the No. 2 propeller shaft flange bolts (D).

# Propeller Shaft Installation

1. Set the No. 2 propeller shaft (A) to the rear differential (B) by aligning the reference mark (C) you made during the removal procedure. Then install new flange bolts (D) to the specified torque.

![](images/4ceef84666340141aea3385b62fafc141ecafbc7b2bba943fb587a9debf68f38.webp)

2. Install new center support bearing mounting bolts (A).

![](images/7f8a0ed2c8dea248a8f9ffe601da74bc28bbdd461eecca0394279720dab431b1.webp)  
10 x1.25 mm 39 Nm (4.0 kgf.m, 29 Ibfft) Replae.

# Propeller Shaft Installation (cont'd)

3. Set the No. 1 propeller shaft (A) to the transfer companion flange (B) by aligning the reference mark (C) you made during the removal procedure. Then install new flange bolts (D) to the specified torque.

![](images/1200ed7defe7b738aa8abbdb24c37e1812395bad445bed36eea9591c33c8868f.webp)

4. Install the propeller shaft protector (A).

![](images/ba1e1a0350cc913139124ffd19b002693eb5f1226ed366d85afd848ed07af47d.webp)

5. If you installed a new propeller shaft, test-drive the vehicle at 55 mph (88 km/h), and check for noise or vibration. If there is a noise or vibration, rotate the propeller shaft 180 degrees from its current alignment with the rear differential companion flange, then recheck.

# SUPPLEMENTAL RESTRAINT SYSTEM (SRS)

The Accord Crosstour/Crosstour V6 SRS includes a driver's airbag in the steering wheel hub, afront passenger's airbag in the dashboard above the glove box, front seat belt tensioners in the front seat belt retractors, side curtain airbags in the sides of the roof, and side airbags in the front seat-backs.Information necessary to safely service the SRS is included in this Service Manual. Items marked with an asterisk \* on the contents page include or are located near SRS components. Servicing, disassembling, or replacing these items requires special precautions and tools, and should be done by an authorized Honda dealer.

To avoid rendering the SRS inoperative, which could lead to personal injury or death in the event of a severe frontal or side collision, al SRS service work should be done by an authorized Honda dealer. Improper service procedures, including incorrect removal and installation of the SRS, could lead to personal injury caused by unintentional deployment of the front airbags, side airbags, side curtain airbags, and/or front seat belt tensioners. Do not bump or impact the SRS unit, front impact sensors, side impact sensors, or rear safing sensor, especiall when the ignition switch is in ON (i), or for at least 3 minutes after the ignition switch is turned to LOCK (0); otherwise, the system may fail in a colision, or the airbags or the tensioners may deploy. SRS electrical connectors are identified by yellow color coding. Related components are located in the steering column, center console, dashboard, dashboard lower cover, in the dashboard above the glove box, in the front seats, in the roof side, and around the floor. Do not use electrical test equipment on these circuits.
