### Steering Wheel Rotational Play Check

1. Set the front wheels in the straight ahead position.

2. Measure how far you can turn the steering wheel left and right without moving the front wheels. If the play is within the limit, the steering gearbox and the steering linkage are OK. If the play exceeds the limit, adjust the rack guide (see page 17-17). If the play is still excessive after rack guide adjustment, do the steering linkage and the steering gearbox (see page 17-6).


### Rotational play:0— 10 mm (0—0.39 in)

![](images/ea64c9801669ce2970385d44dce3a35b55416486d6f74cb18540eb8ab6e4b2f7.webp)


### Power Assist Check

NOTE: This test should be done with original equipment tires and wheels at the correct tire pressure.

1. Check the power steering fluid level (see page 17-28).   
2. Start the engine, let it idle, and turn the steering wheel from lock to lock several times to warm up the fluid.   
3. Attach the spring scale (A) to the steering wheel. With the engine idling and the vehicle on a clean, dry floor, pull the scale as shown, and read it as soon as the tires begin to turn. If the scale reads no more than the specification, the steering gearbox and pump are OK. If the scale reads more than the specification, troubleshoot the steering system (see page 17-24).


### Initial turning load:34 N (3.5 kgf, 7.7 Ibf)

![](images/93cdf6dca5c2b981e3b3caca728ec6005c641679b9a69c2ac88e89f35b2e3428.webp)

![](images/fffa6cf7272b647685657d6b699582e8342a31021bfbe080727e999185113671.webp)


### Steering Wheel Removal

SRS components are located in this area. Review the SRS component locations (see page 24-13), and the precautions and procedures (see page 24-16) before doing repairs or service.

1. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86).   
2. Set the front wheels in the straight ahead position, then remove the driver's airbag from the steering wheel (see page 24-184).   
3. Disconnect the cable reel subharness connector (A).

![](images/7dd4cc3075bf61c426bbad094eca17e7f687fe8fcc5e7055c31773d8a4e1d559.webp)

4. Loosen the steering wheel bolt (B) three turns.

5. Install the steering wheel puller (A) on the steering wheel (B). Free the steering wheel from the steering column shaft by turning the pressure bolt (C) of the puller.

Note these items when removing the steering wheel:

Do not tap on the steering wheel or the steering column shaft when removing the steering wheel. If you thread the puller bolts (D) into the wheel hub more than five threads, the bolts will hit the cable reel and damage it. To prevent this, install a pair of jam nuts five threads up on each puller bolt.

![](images/cba4e97d8d1cc47a10127459eecc7515c2de9fa4f3889d09e285119e964bac69.webp)

6. Remove the steering wheel puller, then remove the steering wheel bolt (A) and the steering wheel from the steering column.

![](images/0fc72340092b0d5bc7cf2edcb47d47dc44d1ccfe6aa5fbab335f3366fd311d22.webp)


### Steering Wheel Disassembly/Reassembly

![](images/b41e12856eeacee8611bc048937e26e85bc8203e3fb18e92499b98443fab01af.webp)

SRS components are located in this area. Review the SRS component locations (see page 24-13), and the precautions and procedures (see page 24-16) before doing repairs or service.

1. Before installing the steering wheel, make sure the front wheels are pointing straight ahead, then center the cable reel (A). Do this by first rotating the cable reel clockwise until it stops. Then rotate it counterclockwise about three full turns. The arrow mark (B) on the cable reel label should point straight up.

![](images/795705fd68f7a3696e19d8676ba85b1dd1dbb45a31fb2a9eb5b386bbc08a27bc.webp)

2. Position the two tabs (A) of the turn signal canceling sleeve (B) as shown. Install the steering wheel on to the steering column shaft, making sure the steering wheel hub (C) engages the pins (D) of the cable reel and tabs of the turn signal canceling sleeve. Do not tap on the steering wheel or steering column shaft when installing the steering wheel.

![](images/dfcca9a15edcd8d0ce15d1319aaf2400a3e43c994079a2ed791681475e1109e9.webp)

3. Install the steering wheel bolt (A), and tighten it to the specified torque. Connect the cable reel subharness connector (B). Make sure the wire harness is routed and fastened properly.

![](images/9fd57f2f35a53b72684d9db981c45bbebf97cf4c236a2887d3d310ff5c21128a.webp)

4. Install the driver's airbag (see page 24-184).

5. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86), and check these items: Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds, and then goes off. Make sure the horn and turn signal switches work properly. Make sure the steering wheel switches work properly.

6. After installation, check the steering wheel spoke angle. If the steering spoke angles to the right and left are not equal (steering wheel is not centered), correct the engagement of the wheel/column shaft splines.


### Steering Column Removal and Installation

SRS components are located in this area. Review the SRS component locations (see page 24-13), and the precautions and procedures (see page 24-16) before doing repairs or service.


### Removal

1. Tilt the steering column all the way down, and move it all the way out.   
2. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86).   
3. Remove the driver's airbag (see page 24-184), and the steering wheel (see page 17-7).   
4. Remove the driver's dashboard undercover (see page 20-135).   
5. Remove the steering column covers (see page 20-151).   
6. Remove the steering joint cover (A).

![](images/d38fb61c72f57ea6c1de8377b8c9c12d4928ae05f727d3dac4742011244adc4c.webp)

7. Loosen the steering joint upper bolt (A), and remove the steering joint lower bolt (B). Disconnect the steering joint (C) by sliding the steering joint into the column shaft (D). Tighten the steering joint upper bolt to hold the steering joint in place.


> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Do not disconnect the steering joint from the column shaft.   
> If the center guide (E) is in place and has not moved, leave it in place.   
> If the center guide has come off discard it.
>
> ![](images/d714eff08787998ba8e8919ad045eb83326d3aa5e2a9189bae97cf16de7f5088.webp)
>
> 8. Disconnect the wire harness connectors from the combination switch assembly/cable reel (A).
>
> ![](images/5e6972735062c8c2716c08ecd7349bb388b694c299a32f297cc6e2a1cecb1a7d.webp)
>
> 9.Remove the combination switch assembly/cable ree from the steering column shaft by removing the screws (B).   
> 10. Disconnect the connectors from the ignition switch, and release the wire harness clips from the steering column.   
> 11.Make sure that the lock lever ( is in the locked position. Remove the steering column (D) by removing the attaching nuts and bolts, and carefully guide it out of the dashboard. NOTE: Do not release the lock lever until the steering column is installed. If the lock lever is released beforehand, adjust the steering column (see page 17-15) after installation.


### Installation

1. Install the steering column in the reverse order of removal, and note these items:

Make sure the wires are not caught or pinched by any parts. Tighten the screws (A) in the sequence shown.

![](images/ee8d483dfaa5d7b17cd14183628235803a7bf663553fcc4cb03d2a8881a1be03.webp)

2. Center the steering rack within its stroke.

3. Loosen the upper steering joint bolt (A), and slip the lower end of the steering joint (B) on to the pinion shaft (C).

NOTE:

Pinion shaft with center guide: Install the steering joint by aligning the center guide (D). Pinion shaft without center guide: Position the steering column by aligning the gap (E) within the angle.

![](images/97dfb24c9805263c51e142bb64d28bbefd6869f0e760543585135377d34fbcef.webp)

4. Align the bolt hole (A) on the steering joint with the groove (B) around the pinion shaft, then loosely install the steering joint lower bolt (C). Be sure that the joint bolt is securely in the groove in the pinion shaft.

![](images/ad76c3d894f6e06d7270f8e2584fcd4982379ad7471d045032ba8ca309e28257.webp)

5. Pull on the steering joint to make sure that the steering joint is fully seated, then tighten the steering joint lower bolt to the specified torque. 6. Tighten the steering joint upper bolt (D) to the specified torque.

7. Install the steering joint cover (A).

![](images/c22110de2b5f9839b7badbd44c0b99e5616092286f8dbb9f1f40f7e636185d37.webp)

8. Install the steering column covers (see page 20-151).

9.Instal the driver's dashboard undercover (see page 20-135).   
10. Install the steering wheel (see page 17-9), and the driver's airbag (see page 24-184).   
11. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86), and check these items: Turn the ignition switch to ON (ll), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds, and then goes off. Make sure the horn and turn signal switches work properly. Make sure the steering wheel switches work properly.

12. After installation, check these items:

Check the steering wheel spoke angle. If the steering spoke angles to the right and left are not equal (steering wheel and rack are not centered), correct the engagement of the joint/pinion shaft splines. Set the steering column to the center tilt position, and to the center telescopic position, then do the front toe inspection (see page 18-5).


### Inspection

1. Remove the steering column (see page 17-10).

2. Check these items:

Check for loose bearing mounting nuts (A), If they are loose, replace the column as an assembly.   
Check the steering column ball bearings and the steering joints  for play and proper movement. I any bearing is noisy or has excessive play, replace the steering column as an assembly.   
Check the sliding capsules (D) for distortion or breakage.  there is distortion or breakage, replace the steering column as an assembly.   
Check the tilt mechanism and telescopic mechanism for movement and damage.   
Apply multipurpose grease to the steering column. NOTÉ: Do not use silicone grease.

![](images/9d49c443ce421781cb53fde47b9b96078710c2d7ba8400d0e5ff1992dd34dc93.webp)

3. Instal the steering column (see page 17-12).


### Check of Telescoping Force

1.Set the steering wheel in the straight ahead driving position, and loosen the lock lever fully. 2. Attach the spring scale (A) to the highest point of the steering wheel, and tilt the steering column to the lowest position.

1. Set the steering wheel in the straight ahead driving position, and loosen the lock lever fully, and push in the steering wheel to the fully telescoped in position. 2. Attach the spring scale (A) to the center point of the steering wheel as shown.

![](images/416b6365e8632eb5378ed8c9678b3ba9c36b3d9efe30e1d9ac44c7c301392cb7.webp)

![](images/1f4a17cef62ebac016288cf0337f5d2cf385043123104b536dd7c4c5245e6167.webp)

3. Pullthe spring scale, and read the force required to move the steering column during telescoping. Telescoping force: Standard: 116 N (11.8 kgf, 26.1 Ibf) max. 4. If the measurement is higher than specified, replace the steering column as an assembly (see page 17-10).

3. Pull the spring scale straight up, and read the force required to move the steering column.   
4. Attach the spring scale to the lowest point of the steering wheel.   
5. Pull the spring scale straight down, and read the force required to move the steering column. Tilting force (upward/downward): Standard: 70 N (7.1 kgf, 15.7 Ibf) max.   
6. If the measurement is higher than specified, or if the tilt function feels rough, do the following:   
-1. Loosen the attaching nuts and bolts so they are finger-tight.   
-2. Release the lock lever, and tilt and telescope the steering column several times.   
-3. Tilt the column down, then tighten the lock lever. -4. Tighten the attaching nuts, then tighten the attaching bolts.   
7. Test the tilting force again. If the force is still higher

than the specification, replace the steering column as an assembly (see page 17-10).


### Check of Lock Lever Force

1. Move the lock lever (A) from the loosened position to the locked position three to five times, then release the lock lever. Adjust the steering column to the center tilt position and also to the full telescopic out position, and hold the steering wheel.'

![](images/78f50eb00459f164721d0a49008e55b2f69bbed6c1a1bfad369109fcd0b02083.webp)

Lock lever force: 77 N (7.9 kgf, 17.3 Ibf) max.

2. Using the push-pull gauge, push up the lock lever 10 mm (0.39 in) in from its end, and measure the force required to move the lock lever.

3. If the measurement is higher than specified, replace the steering column as an assembly (see page 17-10).


### Steering Lock Replacement

1. Remove the steering column (see page 17-10). 2. Center-punch both of the shear bolts (A), and drill their heads off with a 5.0 mm (0.197 in) drill bit. Be careful not to damage the steering lock (B) when removing the shear bolts.

![](images/29d8a2098c3b6a04931895da51b2a88eb0c1e988ae2ca991db069f0c232c6b6d.webp)

3. Remove the shear bolts from the steering lock, then remove the steering lock.   
4. Remove the immobilizer-keyless control unit from the steering lock, then install it on the new steering lock (see page 22-232).   
. Install the steering lock without the key inserted.   
6. Loosely tighten the new shear bolts.   
7. Insert the ignition key, and check for proper operation of the steering wheel lock and that the ignition key turns freely.   
8. Tighten the shear bolts (A) until the hex heads (B) twist off.

![](images/290caaecac52f3de23970f72aa15517c4631717901b07f7b08754eec6958f304.webp)

9. Install the steering column (see page 17-12).

10. Rewrite all new keys to the immobilizer-keyless control unit (see page 22-231), and make sure the immobilizer system works properly.


### Rack Guide Adjustment

Special Tools Required   
Locknut Wrench, 40 mm 07MAA-SL00100 or Locknut   
Wrench, 41 mm 07916-SA50001

1. Set the front wheels in the straight ahead position. 2. Loosen the rack guide screw locknut (A) with the locknut wrench, then remove the rack guide screw (B).

![](images/ec4c866f6af6f7bead7d4bb918104f7111dde329b5dd64355d7e5abc6e34d790.webp)

3. Remove the old sealant from the rack guide screw (A), and apply new sealant (Three Bond 1215 or Loctite 5699) to the middle of the threads (B). Loosely install the rack guide screw on the steering gearbox.

NOTE: If more than 5 minutes have passed after applying the sealant, remove the old sealant and residue, and reapply new sealant.

![](images/ad7aa1f2d76ce7a2ffe44ba001313e6da56452b8b9bfbfb2ea6d978080627dc1.webp)

4. Tighten the rack guide screw (A) to 25 N·m (2.5 kgf.m, 18 Ibf.ft), then loosen it.

![](images/60cc0ba7264ac418fc96770480b9a92ded34fcfed82201a9b7ca05d6722e150f.webp)

5. Retighten the rack guide screw to 5.9 N·m (0.60 kgfm, 4.4 Ibf.ft), then back it off to the specified angle.

Specified return angle: 15±5 °

6. Hold the rack guide screw stationary with a wrench, and tighten the locknut (B) by hand until it's fully seated.   
7. Install the locknut wrench on the locknut, and hold the rack guide screw stationary with a wrench. Tighten the locknut to the specified torque.   
8. Check for unusual steering effort through the complete turning range.   
9. Check the steering wheel rotational play (see page 17-5) and the power assist (see page 17-5).


### Special Tools Required

Bearing Driver Attachment, 36 07965-SA50500

1. Disconnect the tie-rod end ball joint from the knuckle (see step 33 on page 17-44).   
2. Remove the tie-rod end from the rack end (see page 17-49).   
3. Remove the ball joint boot from the tie-rod end, and wipe the old grease off the ball pin.   
4. Pack the lower area of the ball pin (A) with fresh multipurpose grease.

![](images/ae1fee765e1f1a61aee27809e5b9a8c47413c3b09ed8d06db9a5cb1d5a21a8ac.webp)

5. Pack the interior of the new ball joint boot (B) and lip (C) with fresh multipurpose grease.

Note these items when installing new grease:

Keep grease off the boot mounting area (D) and the tapered section (E) of the ball pin. Do not allow dust, dirt, or other foreign materials to enter the boot.

6. Install the ball joint boot (A) using the bearing driver attachment. The boot must not have a gap at the boot installation sections (B). After installing the boot, check the ball pin tapered section for grease contamination, and wipe it if necessary.

![](images/484ba40df597d148f003a32aafff8eb95157894dc864225854e0a60124198c71.webp)

7. Install the tie-rod end to the rack end (see page 17-49).   
8. Connect the tie-rod end ball joint to the knuckle (see step 30 on page 17-67).   
9. Check the wheel alignment, and adjust it if necessary (see page 18-5).


### Gearbox Mount Cushion Replacement

1. Remove the steering gearbox (see page 17-39). 2. Position a 40 mm socket (A) on the flange part of the gearbox housing with a washer (B), a 10 x 150 mm flange bolt (C), and a 10 mm nut (D) as shown.

![](images/1c5d75b9fc6cb1446ba57658a2d7c7d89ab0d0037afdd61efbbfff62a8cec8fa.webp)

3. Hold the flange bolt with a wrench, and tighten the nut with a wrench. Remove the gearbox mount cushion (E).

4. Apply a mild soap and water solution to the new gearbox mount cushion surface (A), then place the mount cushion on the gearbox mounting cushion hole.

6. Install the gearbox mount cushion by tightening the nut until the mount cushion edge (A) properly fits on the gearbox flange surface (B).

![](images/fb9c5caebb796ab023377b16889a034616bc3c1464a749a67fe889f1dd6bf1f8.webp)

5. Position a 40 mm socket (B) on the flange part of the gearbox housing with a washer, a flange bolt, and a nut as shown.

![](images/9aea01a904174c091406a3439731a096048651668c66231629bbd60850f67277.webp)

7. Install the steering gearbox (see page 17-64).

### Hard Steering

6. Check for a bent rack shaft or misadjusted rack guide (too tight).

NOTE:

Compare to a known-good vehicle that is the same trim level.   
Check for suspension damage.   
Check the steering alignment.   
Check the tire condition and pressure.

Is the rack shaft bent or the rack guide adjusted too tight?

YES–Replace the rack shaft, or readjust the rack guide preload (see page 17-17).

NO—Faulty valve body unit. Overhaul the valve body unit (see page 17-49).

1. Check the power assist (see page 17-5).

Is the initial turning load more than 34 N (3.5 kgf, 7.7 Ibf)?

YES–Do the pump pressure test with T/N 07406-0010001 (see page 17-25), T/N 07406-001000A or T/N 07406-001A101 (see page 17-26). If the pressure test is within specification, go to step 2.

NO–Power assist is OK at this time. Compare to a known-good vehicle.

2. Using a spring scale, measure the power assist in both directions, to the left and to the right.

Are the two measurements within 5.0 N (0.51 kgf, 1.12 Ibf) of each other?

YES–Go to step 3.

NO-Go to step 5.

3. Measure the fluid pressure with both pressure gauge valves open (if so equipped), while turning the steering wheel fully to the left and fully to the right.

Is the pressure 8,830 —9,310 kPa (90.04 — 94.93 kgf/cm², 1,280.7 — 1,350.3 psi) or more in both directions?

YES–Go to step 4.

NO–Faulty steering gearbox. Overhaul the steering gearbox (see page 17-49).

4. Adjust the rack guide (see page 17-17), and retest.

Is the steering OK?

YES-Repair is completed.

NO–Faulty steering gearbox. Overhaul the steering gearbox (see page 17-49).

5. Check the cylinder lines for deformation (see page 17-29).

Are any of the line(s) deformed?

YES–Replace the deformed line(s).

NO-Go to step 6.


### Special Tools Required

. P/S Joint Adapter (Pump) 07VAK-P8A011A • P/S Joint Adapter Plate (Pump) 07VAK-P8A012B • Hose Joint Adapter 07RAK-S040122 • P/S Pressure Gauge 07406-0010001

Check the fluid pressure as follows to determine whether the trouble is in the pump or steering gearbox.

1. Check the power steering fluid level (see page 17-28).

2.Disconnect the pump outlet hose (A) from the pump outlet with care so as not to spill the power steering fluid on the frame and other parts, then install the P/S joint adapter (pump) on the pump outlet (B) with the P/S joint adapter plate (pump).

![](images/317921b1740b577f820551ae165016353e3df2bc69e996008e6005aa6dc8038f.webp)

3. Connect the hose joint adapter to the P/S pressure gauge, then connect the pump outlet hose to the hose joint adapter.   
4. Install the P/S pressure gauge to the P/S joint adapter (pump).

5. Oen the shut-off valve (A) fully.

![](images/ccb7913ef0a9878af499ee3b60dea148411c6f16acc230cb7740f230a9fbe0e2.webp)

6. Open the pressure control valve (B) fully.

7. Start the engine, and let it idle.

8. Turn the steering wheel from lock to lock several times to warm the fluid to operating temperature at 158 °F (70 °C).

9. Measure steady-state fluid pressure while the engine is idling. The gauge should read no more than 1,470 kPa (14.99 kgf/cm², 213.2 psi).

If the reading is high, check for:

Clogged or deformed inlet or return line between the pump and the steering gearbox. Clogged valve body unit.

10. Close the shut-off valve, then close the pressure control valve gradually until the pressure gauge needle is stable. Read the pressure.


### NOTICE

Do not keep the shut-off valve closed more than 5 seconds or the pump could be damaged by over-heating.

11. Immediately open the shut-off valve fully. If the pump is in good condition, the gauge should read at least 8,830 —9,310 kPa (90.04— 94.93 kgf/cm², 1,280.7 — 1,350.3 psi). A low reading means the pump output is too low for full assist. Repair or replace the ритр.


### Special Tools Required

. P/S Joint Adapter (Pump) 07VAK-P8A011A • P/S Joint Adapter Plate (Pump) 07VAK-P8A012B • Hose Joint Adapter 07RAK-S040122 • P/S Pressure Gauge 07406-001000A or 07406-001A101

Check the fluid pressure as follows to determine whether the trouble is in the pump or steering gearbox.

1. Check the power steering fluid level (see page 17-28).

2. Disconnect the pump outlet hose (A) from the pump outlet with care so as not to spill the power steering fluid on the frame and other parts, then install the P/S joint adapter (pump) on the pump outlet (B) with the P/S joint adapter plate (pump).

![](images/4a13e9ddd795878d768af267a7fc0a6bd7da117437b6ae6d9893c641cb9ca1d9.webp)

3. Connect the hose joint adapter to the P/S pressure gauge, then connect the pump outlet hose to the hose joint adapter.   
4. Install the P/S pressure gauge to the P/S joint adapter (pump).

5. Open the shut-off valve (A) fully.

![](images/33e7ed46798a3af5f36b377b05eaa11d9de76476e5d4b730471f3c6ad1fbfbde.webp)

6. Start the engine, and let it idle.

7. Turn the steering wheel from lock to lock several times to warm the fluid to operating temperature at 158 °F (70 °C).

8. Measure steady-state fluid pressure while the engine is idling. The gauge should read no more than 1,470 kPa (14.99 kgf/cm², 213.2 psi).

If the reading is high, check for:

Clogged or deformed inlet or return line between the pump and the steering gearbox. Clogged valve body unit.

9. Let the engine idle, and gradually close the shut-off valve and immediately read the pressure.


### NOTICE

Do not keep the shut-off valve closed more than 5 seconds or the pump could be damaged by over-heating.

10. Immediately open the shut-off valve fully. If the pump is in good condition, the gauge should read at least 8,830—9,310 kPa (90.04—94.93 kgf/cm², 1,280.7— 1,350.3 psi). A low reading means the pump output is too low for full assist. Repair or replace the pиmp.

PUMP ASSEMBLY

![](images/1ddbdfabd84183c88fb58876743c076a4734ce641b01ccff1f5298bccaf172cf.webp)

HOSES and LINES Inspect hoses for damage, leaks, interference, and twisting. Inspect fluid lines for damage, rusting, and leaks. Check for leaks at hose and the line joints, and at the connections.


### Replacement

1. Check the reservoir (A) at regular intervals, and add the recommended fluid as necessary. Always use Honda Power Steering Fluid. Using any other type of power steering fluid or automatic transmission fluid can cause increased wear, fluid leaks, and poor steering in cold weather.

NOTE: If the fluid is contaminated, the screen in the reservoir may be partiallý blocked. Inspect the reservoir screen for any debris. If the reservoir screen is clogged, replace the reservoir, and check for the source of the contamination.

System capacity: 1.1 L (1.2 US qt) at disassembly   
Reservoir capacity: 0.32 L (0.34 US qt)

![](images/4e6b46e4b14ecb512ebb781ff70ee048d0e9652324e302b97013d916ad5c15b8.webp)

2. Remove the reservoir from its holder. Raise the reservoir, then disconnect the return hose (A) to drain the reservoir. Take care not to spill the fluid on the vehicle. Wipe off any spilled fluid at once.

NOTE: Inspect the reservoir screen for any debris. If the reservoir screen is clogged, replace the reservoir, and check for the source of the contamination.

![](images/4a5dffca77a391b471f3de6dd77d88040d080a7b5aa41b494650f425d7e1d5b5.webp)

3. Connect a hose (B) of suitable diameter to the disconnected return hose, and put the hose end in a suitable container.

4. Start the engine, let it run at idle, and turn the steering wheel from lock to lock several times. When fluid stops running out of the hose, shut off the engine. Discard the fluid.

NOTE: Stop the engine immediately once the fluid stops running out of the hose to prevent pump damage.

5. Reinstall the return hose on the reservoir.

6. Fill the reservoir to the upper level line (C).

7. Start the engine, and run it at idle. Turn the steering from lock to lock several times to bleed air from the system.

8. Recheck the fluid level, and add some if necessary. Do not fill the reservoir beyond the upper level line.

9. If the fluid is contaminated, dark, or discolored, repeat the procedure as necessary until the system is clean.


### Power Steering Hose, Line, and Pressure Switch Replacement

Note these items during instalation:

Connect each hose to the corresponding line securely until it contacts the stop on the line. Install the clamp or adjustable clamp at the specified distance from the hose end as shown. Check allclamps for deterioration or deformation; replace the clamps with new ones if necessary. Add the recommended power steering fluid to the specified level on the reservoir, and check for leaks.

![](images/314ed0c074868d2cb9f8d6115e0bf86ccbf7d960b9485a0f41d178029523b2f6.webp)

2. Place a suitable container under the vehicle.   
3. Drain the power steering fluid from the reservoir (see page 17-28).   
4. Cover the auto-tensioner, the alternator, and the A/C compressor with several shop towels to protect them from spilled power steering fluid.   
5. Disconnect the pump outlet hose (A) from the pump, then remove the O-ring (B).


> ℹ️ **Примечание:**

### Pump Replacement

1. Remove the engine cover (see step 1 on page 4-20).   
2. Place a suitable container under the vehicle to catch any spilled fluid.   
3. Drain the power steering fluid from the reservoir (see page 17-28).   
4. Remove the drive belt (A) from the pump pulley: '10 model (see page 4-30), '11-12 models (see page 4-31)   
5. Cover the auto-tensioner, the alternator, and the A/C compressor with several shop towels to protect them from spilled power steering fluid. Disconnect the pump inlet hose (B) and the pump outlet hose (C) from the pump (D), and plug them. Take care not to spill the fluid on the vehicle. Wipe off any spilled fluid at once. Do not turn the steering wheel with the pump removed.   
6. Remove the pump mounting bolts (E), then remove the pump.   
7. Cover the opening of the pump to prevent foreign material from entering the pump.   
8. Transfer the pump inlet hose and the pump outlet hose from the original pump onto the new pump with a new O-ring (F).   
9. Loosely install the pump in the pump bracket with the mounting bolts, then tighten the pump fittings to the specified torque.   
10. Tighten the pump mounting bolts to the specified torque.

![](images/0d67065f5e7c01005d1fc7f884f725465f9a0286ac65e21b20c81c44fd304a9e.webp)

11. Instal the drive belt (A): '10 model (see page 4-30), '11-12 models (see page 4-31)

Note these items during drive belt instalation:

Inspect the belt for wear and cracks. Replace the belt if necessary.   
Make sure that the belt is properly positioned on the pulleys (B).   
Do not get power steering fluid or grease on the auto-tensioner, the alternator, the A/C compressor, and the drive belt or pulley faces. Clean off any fluid or grease before installation.

![](images/834b32714cdcc19768ff0e0934c4d122c7129fa14896707a7b02e31f8960d6d0.webp)

12. Install the engine cover (see page 4-20). 13. Fill the reservoir to the upper level line (see page 17-28). 14. Start the engine, and check for leaks (see page 17-27).


### Exploded View

![](images/e0489b2948cb0ac88e370b45606f637e9c5e94f2964cbc7416fa180c836ea97b.webp)


### Pump Overhaul (cont'd)

Special Tools Required   
Pulley Holder 07ZAB-S5A0100   
• Bearing Driver Attachment, 28 x 30 07946-1870100   
•Driver Handle, 15 x 135L 07749-0010000

NOTE: Refer to the Exploded View as needed during the following procedure.


### Disassembly

1. Remove the power steering pump (see page 17-32).   
2. Drain the remaining fluid from the power steering риmp.   
3. Hold the power steering pump (A) in a vise with soft jaws (B), then hold the pulley (C) with the pulley holder (D), and remove the pulley nut (E) and pulley. Be careful not to damage the pump housing with the jaws of a vise.   
4. Remove the inlet joint and the 14.8 mm O-ring.   
5. Loosen the flow control valve cap with a hex wrench, and remove the cap, the 16.7 mm O-ring, the flow control valve spring, and the flow control valve.   
6. Remove the pump cover and the pump cover seal.   
7. Remove the outer side plate, the cam ring, the rotor, the vanes, the side plate, the 15.2 mm O-ring, and the 51.0 mm O-ring.   
8. Remove the snap ring, then remove the subvalve from the pump housing.   
9. Remove the 40mm snap ring, then remove the driveshaft by tapping the shaft end with a soft face hammer.   
10. Remove the pump seal from the pump housing.

![](images/0279f0eb3f93c3d873c429b90125ae7e2cf2717d1fe7cec61b8a8e953b5acc09.webp)


### Inspection

11. Check the flow control valve for wear, burrs, and other damage to the edges of the grooves in the valve.

12. Inspect the bore of the flow control valve on the pump housing for scratches and wear.   
13. Slip the flow control valve (A) back in the pump housing, and check that it moves in and out smoothly. If OK, go to step 14; if not, replace the pump as an assembly. The flow control valve is not available separately.

![](images/56a870c2c660c4ed142239dcab9b19721a6c07a163b99005eba322fc542cfc96.webp)

14. Attach a hose (A) to the end of the flow control valve (B) as shown. Then submerge the flow control valve in a container of power steering fluid (C), and apply compressed air in the hose. If air bubbles leak through the valve at less than 98 kPa (1.00 kgf/cm², 14.2 psi), replace the pump as an assembly. The flow control valve is not available separately. If the flow control valve is OK, set it aside for reassembly later.

![](images/bcaf77fe476841ee87746deeedbd22b53ae55907cae6afe584e154fb304b2e6a.webp)

15. Inspect the ball bearing by rotating the outer race slowly. If you feel any play (axial or radial) or roughness, remove the faulty ball bearing (A), and install a new ball bearing (B).

![](images/6e895ac390158e3e11f07370f61383b139af98c2ae65d3e54ca6a0fe3b7ffac0.webp)

16. Inspect the driveshaft by rotating the inner race slowly. If you feel any play (axial or radial), remove the worn driveshaft (C), and install a new driveshaft (D).


### Reassembly

17. Align the pin (A) of the subvalve (B) with the oil passage (C) in the pump housing, and push the subvalve into place, then install the snap ring (D).

![](images/0ef259ce6465cbe48aac41e56c28f5ba4d739be9096139cbc1f402dece5a42b1.webp)

18. Install the new pump seal (A) (with its grooved side facing in) into the pump housing (B) by hand first, then drive it in using the driver handle (C) and bearing driver attachment (D) until there is no step at the top of the pump seal, and the seal is fully seated in the pump housing.

![](images/b0d2b80cbdd16a463d40898e427b92168e8b725757e88b09f4d049bdb4452a7f.webp)

19. Position the driveshaft (A) in the pump housing, then press it in with the appropriate size socket (B) as shown.

![](images/694fb6d978c43dfe0eec554b01fa281669a70412e1314fb5a87a260d4404ed6c.webp)

20. Install the 40 mm snap ring (C) with its beveled edge facing out.   
21.Coat the new pump cover seal (A) with power steering fluid, and install t into the groove in the pump cover (B).

![](images/67944a3508eb5599f83404477c79b461c308c020378cfbf05fcae4394791e164.webp)

22. Install the outer side plate (C) over the two roll pins (D) with the groove (E) facing up.

23. Set the cam ring (A) over the two roll pins with the "." mark (B) facing down.

![](images/63e0164f05552b684fbfd8d9e17c2a6172341e5c7bea1a8b1b7a05aef7f4e129.webp)

24. Install the rotor (A) to the pump cover (B).

![](images/8966d6e771fb05578660a7afb2f2e852861d528093cbab9e979e257b3fa78c7e.webp)

25. Set the 10 vanes (C) in the grooves in the rotor. Make sure that the round ends (D) of the vanes are in contact with the sliding surface of the cam ring.

26. Coat the new 15.2 mm O-ring (A) with power steering fluid, and install it into the groove in the side plate (B).

![](images/cbb5bb9827197ce6246dd55f46af3437cb620d31602771e98bd88b8ebb1bb24d.webp)

27. Install the side plate on the cam ring (C) by aligning the roll pin set holes (D) in the side plate with the roll pins (E).   
28.Coat the new 51.0 mm O-ring (A) with power steering fluid, and position it in the bottom of the pump housing.

![](images/52671cb918a209fc8313a160f9a0ec9a5ec6bb92ce032233efe4f63735c59a8a.webp)

29. Install the pump cover assembly (B) in the pump housing. Tighten the bolts to the specified torque alternating in two or more steps.


### Pump Overhaul (cont'd)

30. Coat the flow control valve (A) with power steering fluid, then installit and the flow control valve spring (B) in the pump housing.

![](images/1962b5c74a9a2c40cd541795609d51b0d19a5a50e14cb2ac72e270692a892665.webp)

31. Coat the new 16.7 mm O-ring (C) with power steering fluid, and install it on the flow control valve cap (D), then install the cap on the pump housing. Tighten it to the specified torque.   
32. Coat the new 14.8 mm O-ring (A) with power steering fluid, and install it on the inlet joint (B). Install the inlet joint on the pump housing.

![](images/9dc4e1daa6f0f7eea7758ca1d7440751ab9b69b7a0b7e65ffc43fc65ca4ae52a.webp)

33. Install the pulley (A), then loosely install the pulley nut (B). Hold the steering pump in a vise with soft jaws (C). Be careful not to damage the pump housing with the jaws of a vise.

![](images/65aaddc3bbb852a4038fafa6b004f6e6f956dd83e91c5666ebbf91d02e42ba90.webp)

34. Hold the pulley with the pulley holder (D), and tighten the pulley nut to the specified torque.   
35. Check that the pump turns smoothly by turning the pulley by hand. If it turns hard, loosen the four flange bolts on the cover, then retighten them in the same manner as in step 28. Retest. If the pump is still hard to turn, replace the pump.

36. Reinstall the power steering pump (see page 17-32).


### Special Tools Required

•Engine Support Hanger, A and Reds AAR-T1256\* •Engine Hanger Balance Bar VSB02C000019\*   
Attachment Arm SlL02C000033\*   
Ball Joint Thread Protector, 12 mm 07AAF-SDAA100 Ball Joint Remover, 28 mm 07MAC-SL0A202   
•Ball Joint Remover, 32 mm 07MAC-SL0A102   
Ball Joint Thread Protector, 14 mm 07AAE-SJAA100 •Subframe Adapter VSB02C000016\*   
\*: Available through the Honda Tool and Equipment Program, 888-424-6857.

Note these items during removal:

Using clean solvent and a brush, wash any oil and dirt off the valve body unit, it's lines, and the end of the steering gearbox. Blow dry with compressed air.   
Lower the front subframe from the body, and remove the steering gearbox through the gap produced by lowering the front subframe.   
The illustrations show 4WD.

1. Pry the passenger's side hood support strut clip, and release the passenger's side hood support strut from the pivot bolt (see page 20-212).

2. Remove the driver's side hood support strut bracket (A), then use it as shown to prop the hood in the wide-open position.


> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Turn the hood support strut bracket inside out. Do not attempt to close the hood with the support strut in the vertical position, as it will damage the support strut and the rod.
>
> ![](images/f7cc74530b51e9de0c596faab2d24c5898ed270df916f05d44c7d8b8cfed86a7.webp)
>
> 3. Drain the power steering fluid (see page 17-28). 4. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86). 5. Raise and support the vehicle (see page 1-12).
>
> 6. Remove the front wheels.
>
> 7. Remove the steering joint cover (A).
>
> ![](images/af98dfaca6faf1f9cfbe243fe9e498a119717b681ec1f8e3eb22473a4a1f8d76.webp)
>
> 8. Loosen the steering joint upper bolt (A), and remove the steering joint lower bolt (B). Disconnect the steering joint (C) by sliding the steering joint into the column shaft (D). Tighten the steering joint upper bolt " to hold the column shaft.
>
> NOTE: Do not disconnect the steering joint from the column shaft.
>
> ![](images/2da89b9fe642907aaedce52cfa3c51f32ae6738fa5adff0af1b64620fd4e89f9.webp)


### Steering Gearbox Removal (cont'd)

9. Center the steering wheel spokes, and install a commercially available steering wheel holder tool (A).

![](images/63f31f1afc0af99f4f03d1044e123a3e9315cca825477521e6529df816b5a70b.webp)

10. Remove the center guide (A) (if equipped) from the top of the pinion shaft (B).

![](images/fe7335533ece8c5cd048f5057337a209ef19cb5730cd8ea153cf618e3567aa1b.webp)

11. Wrap vinyl tape over the splines on the pinion shaft.   
12. Remove the engine cover (see step 1 on page 4-20).   
13. Remove the front grille cover (see page 20-230).   
14. Remove the strut brace (see page 20-261).

15. Remove the pump outlet hose clamp bolt (A).

![](images/69f2c27a300d4939a18b483bebd19384ec47c6ad0b052e4c4f85070df741d17c.webp)

16. Remove the power steering heat shield (A).

![](images/84fcd8615824eb53b3eb973bcdf27561284b5d29cf8c91adfb23dcd64b3ca216.webp)

17. Remove the connector bracket (A) from the front cylinder head; use the bracket bolt hole to attach the engine hanger balance bar front arm.

![](images/f552feabd7b5be99f5a653e8f04fd3f8afd23a62130cbf6814a4ee6d5b7a1faf.webp)

18. Remove the harness clamp bracket (A) from the rear cylinder head; use the bracket bolt hole to attach the 2008 V6 attachment arm (SlL02Co00033).

![](images/345b37b5c46f9bbd58ebf5fe9c99bc7bf11f9d091322d058f61c8d62c8abd4bd.webp)

19. Install the engine hanger balance bar (A). Attach the front arm (B) to the front cylinder head with several spacers (C) and a 10 x 1.25 mm bolt (D). Remove the rear arm from the engine hanger balance bar, then install the 2008 V6 attachment arm (E). Attach the 2008 V6 attachment arm to the rear cylinder head with a spacer (F) and an 8 x 1.25 mm bolt (G).


> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Be careful when working around the windshield.   
> Be careful not to damage the hood opener cable when installing the engine support hanger (H) at the front bulkhead.   
> AAR-T1256 two sets required for stacking additional cross section bar.
>
> ![](images/01333d89ae60604d92dc97cad74038b5cb5d8676a0386ef1c88cb2356280afc8.webp)
>
> 20. Install the engine support hanger onto the vehicle, and attach the hook to the engine balancer bar slot. Tighten the wing nut (Il) by hand, and lift and support the engine.


### Steering Gearbox Removal (cont'd)

21. Remove the front engine mount stop (A), then remove the front engine mount bolt (B).

![](images/d988c99c28ff67a5813bada873d6f9d04493857e445ca8aeda9911d5f6ba2f6d.webp)

22. Disconnect the rear engine mount actuator connector (A).

![](images/e1dc680b2d4a244cc9b911b0116ea30a981358a36a9daeee93c2014f1b18c3ba.webp)

23. Remove the rear engine mount actuator harness clip (A) from the stiffener plate (B) on the driver's side of the steering gearbox.

![](images/4393bfd6fcdb38daf8f66f0ec3fa2357619ac7ac53ae55ddf15791bc789e2f4b.webp)

24. Remove the rear engine mount stop (A).

![](images/9da922880fde24dab543c17b9c5572cf4934da7ef5a960af323c46a4cc10d1cf.webp)

25. Remove the rear engine mount (A).

![](images/1446d69b82948840e7f85ef8fff224b36e3f81d953ffb787ee17464dfd510e5a.webp)

26. Remove the rear engine mount upper bracket (A) from the base bracket.

![](images/f21e99b60f0e63cf6b3e3db40a640ca45267e61b9ae6ffa79a8fa9f618f040c8.webp)

27. Remove the inlet line clamp bolt (A), and disconnect the inlet line (B).

![](images/10bd2f14e01703a8c2145092ccbeebe6859a18b162a3aed8e6380c44935c5b07.webp)

28. Remove the return line clamp bolt (C). Loosen the adjustable hose clamp (D), then disconnect the return hose (E).

29. Remove the inlet line clamp bolt (A).

![](images/f748cc1eea246c3c4b6e1d0167cc05744f50aebf21bb50783ae444d11615b8e2.webp)

30. Release the return hose clamps (B), and remove the return hose (C).


### Steering Gearbox Removal (cont'd)

31. Remove the return line clamp bolt (A).

![](images/87f1378cc524cf3181eeabee36224bd9166ae7d878b7ac4a0b15d10fd57a787e.webp)

32. Release the return line clamp (B), and remove the return line (C).

33. Remove the cotter pin (A) from the tie-rod end ball joint, then remove the nut (B) on both sides.

![](images/90ba394b516fd97746841af309bb4ca7ccbbcb82fbfcdb335fb2c2231e7586e0.webp)

34. Disconnect the tie-rod end ball joint from the knuckle using the ball joint thread protector (C) and the ball joint remover (D) (see page 18-11).

NOTE: Be careful not to damage the ball joint boot when installing the remover.

35. Remove the flange bolts from the passenger's side of the steering gearbox, then remove the gearbox mounting bracket (A) and the mounting cushion (B).

![](images/39e684cf3983d6bca2d56a34031d47846f94af1973e90f409dde781c443c068b.webp)

36. Remove the mounting bolts (A) and the flange bolts (B) from the driver's side of the steering gearbox, and remove the stiffener plates (C) and the washers (D).

![](images/534e623a1066a2771cf4fdb236f7045b1b127650629f7a6dbf4edc2e9d68c5b9.webp)

37. Raise the vehicle.

38. Remove the engine undercover (see page 20-252).

39. Disconnect the front engine mount actuator connector (A).

![](images/1b28d0d9829373289d383ad431db2b0d24bbd5edc9342c9a1b83d8e3ecb276fb.webp)

40. Remove exhaust pipe A:   
2WD (see page 9-11)   
4WD (see page 9-12)

41. 4WD: Remove the propeller shaft (see page 16-40).

42. Remove the cotter pin (A) from the knuckle bal joint, then remove the castle nut (B) on both sides.

![](images/759d1ebe104cc5b77ef6cebbb558e5efaae15d5d9da8b10ee2e7342df59db9db.webp)  
14 x 1.5 mm

43. Disconnect the knuckle ball joint from the lower arm using the ball joint thread protector (C) and the ball joint remover (D) (see page 18-11).


> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Be careful not to damage the bal joint boot when installing the remover.   
> Do not force or hammer on the lower arm, or pry between the lower arm and the knuckle. You could damage the ball joint.
>
> 44. Remove the damper fork mounting nut (A) while holding the mounting bolt (B), then remove the mounting bolt on both sides.
>
> ![](images/e6b434c45b013215fe79f3c4a317ab28cf6f20a13d06f508d84c519950490f22.webp)  
> 12x1.25 mm Replace
>
> 45. Attach the subframe adapter (A) to the front subframe by looping the strap (B) over the front of the subframe, then secure the strap with the stop (C), then tighten the wing nut (D).
>
> ![](images/3fbdb8164796d5f817839008bb5580e8f84bf6ab9831b61dea6993a8c7b66f98.webp)
>
> 46. Raise the jack, and line up the slots in the arms with the bolt holes on the corner of the jack base, then attach them with the bolts and nuts.


### Steering Gearbox Removal (cont'd)

47. Remove the front subframe middle mount (A) on both sides.

![](images/9a025646b8507034523e4aa3f8146390e9412f01591c8282d68608d584579d7a.webp)

48. Remove the flange nuts (A) from the lower transmission mount.

![](images/ad839c686271a681d2c3d5bff7364a1d906fba7d6f4fbbab5880301028927834.webp)

49. Remove the front stiffener mounting bolts (A) from the subframe front stiffeners (B).

![](images/82aa3295ba47d17eab6f02cb26bd17b1652e695e730075f993ef6f31d8e76db8.webp)

50. Loosen the subframe mounting bolts (C) so they are about 20 mm (0.79 in) from the mounting surface. Do not loosen the subframe mounting bolts more than necessary.   
51. Remove the rear stiffener mounting bolts (A) and subframe mounting bolts (B) from the subframe rear stiffeners (C).

![](images/616ed68394f05ee2a3b8f0c70372b19758afd48ced52b6050e133864759035f6.webp)

52. Lower the jack slowly until the front subframe has dropped about 70 mm (2.76 in).

54. Remove the steering gearbox (A) through the fenderwell opening on the driver's side.

![](images/3ec4b397ba996035e529b2e8f078c59a821b67cb487bfd78f1006dec8516b63a.webp)

![](images/0a0b2a191a3a0484d1799eddbaa802690b9ff7d8849ebc58985f1a72e3c2f43e.webp)

55. Remove the pinion shaft grommet (A) from the top of the valve housing.

53. Carefully move the steering gearbox (A) toward the driver's side until the pinion shaft clears the fenderwell opening on the body.

![](images/e87f37a5d260e4ef3a7e6bd352fe75bfc6b489f7e73a395289c71deb9ca4cc3b.webp)

![](images/820bcf2e922c2cc283154eb9f835613561775bd06529f82c8b9790e24d5b0aed.webp)


### Steering Gearbox Removal (cont'd)

56. Remove the return line joint (A) if necessary.

![](images/5166fc624fd76c77feb73d2ac582214d034bba0f9be6053d5dc43170b0be1d23.webp)

57. After removing the steering gearbox, make sure that no power steering fluid gets on the gearbox mount cushions, the gearbox housing, the surface of the front subframe, and the stiffener. Wipe off any spilled fluid at once.

NOTE: Refer to the Exploded View as needed during the following procedure.


### Disassembly

1. Remove the steering gearbox (see page 17-39). 2. Remove both tie-rod ends from the rack ends. 3. Drill a 4.0 mm (0.158 in) diameter hole about 2.5 – 3.0 mm (0.098— 0.118 in) in depth in the staked points (A) on the end plug (B) and the gearbox housing (C).

![](images/ce89494db6aa6e0dc7f5278846afca839d1ef71b49cf242c15e560a02fb77674.webp)

4. Remove the end plug (A) from the gearbox housing, then remove the self-locking nut (B) from the pinion shaft end.

![](images/3de7d466bf3b878153a19ef845840c155f0b124a08c7763cf3a4f9fd50bf6ddb.webp)

5. Remove the boot band (A) and tie-rod clip (B). Pull the boot away from the end of the steering gearbox. Repeat this step for the other side.

![](images/dfee014151c96957241a3190098f0ec0965f4bccbe27df4d1fa699ea80aa0981.webp)

6. Hold the gearbox housing using a C-clamp (A) and wooden blocks (B) to a work bench as shown. Do not clamp the cylinder part of the gearbox housing in a vise.

![](images/fffaf10bccd7987ce090dc1407ba6c025daa595768be8a65baae9ef83af40d1b.webp)


### 7. Unbend the lock washer (A).

![](images/174253a5d636053d9fab4f8dde2b68f4381eaace823b0199ebc6cbca98b7bba5.webp)

8. Hold the flat surface sections (A) of the steering rack (B) with one wrench, and unscrew rack end (C) with another wrench. Be careful not to damage the rack surface with the wrench.

![](images/5efe6d6e9634c1df658427cfbca6fa84e4d9ab9f66351a50483793ad8a49af9d.webp)

9. Remove the lock washer (D) and rubber stop (E). Repeat steps 7 thru 9 for the other side.   
10. Loosen the locknut (A), then remove the rack guide screw (B).

![](images/0389640a843ef29fbba399d48b429b2566fa29d3dd9b37c18b39073c8151f203.webp)

11. Remove the disc washer (C), the spring (D), and the rack guide (E) from the gearbox housing.


### Steering Gearbox Overhaul (cont'd)

12. Remove cylinder line A and B from the steering gearbox.

![](images/e0495a7945d96b423cc6ff9494d3e7bc7c42a5ec200a58e16e19de9329640881.webp)

13. Drain the fluid from the cylinder fittings by slowly moving the steering rack back and forth.   
14. Remove the flange bolts, then remove the valve body unit (A) from the gearbox housing (B). Remove the O-ring (C).

![](images/e3e69ce03048263385430bc587001be554653fedd75b11fb46aba60fe2d74544.webp)

15. Wrap vinyl tape (A) over the end of the steering rack and the gearbox housing. Drill a 3.0 —4.0 mm (0.118—0.158 in) diameter hole about 2.5 —3.0 mm (0.098—0.118 in) in depth in the staked point (B) on the cylinder. Do not allow metal shavings to enter the cylinder side on the gearbox housing. After removing the cylinder end (C), remove any burrs at the staked point.

NOTE: Wrap vinyl tape (D) over the drill and do not drill the depth more than necessary.

![](images/980491b01b4799a1fce5dcdc3320ccf92a8d95feddd2f98fac8f0daa4adec7cc.webp)

16. Hold the gearbox housing using a C-clamp (A) and wooden blocks (B) to a work bench as shown. Do not clamp the cylinder part of the gearbox housing in a vise. Remove the vinyl tape. Then remove the cylinder end (C).

![](images/6b35ccd9e19dec418b758804de5ca67f63218c24fbcfa2536854a97109ea618b.webp)

17. Install a commercially available bearing separator (A) on the gearbox housing as shown.

![](images/a9fbf1caf29de41fe4b84f63cb3a35c9fab8431d5e5ed6c15a46fbba9a110db0.webp)

18. Place an appropriate size deep socket (B) on the steering rack ().

19. Set the steering gearbox in a press so the gearbox housing side points upward, then press the cylinder end seal (D) and steering rack out of the steering gearbox. Hold the steering rack to keep it from falling when pressed clear. Be careful not to damage the inner surface of the cylinder side on the gearbox. housing with the tool.

20. Carefully pry the piston seal ring (A) and O-ring (B) off the rack piston. Be careful not to damage the inside of the seal ring groove and piston edges when removing the seal ring.

![](images/72a93586332a3d8130ae64969910b1e8bb2388989563907f370a42c8518c42b0.webp)

21. Turn the cylinder end seal remover attachment (A) so it fits through the rack guide hole of the gearbox housing, then position the seal remover on the backup ring (B). Make sure that the seal remover is securely positioned on the backup ring.

![](images/554d06e693ea1ed1fb40479ce27051fe17e4674b4e6fe9f466bf1571fb166c55.webp)

22. Insert a 24" long 3/8" drive extension (A), on the cylinder end seal remover attachment (B). Place the gearbox housing in a press, then remove the backup ring (C) and cylinder end seal (D) from the gearbox housing by pressing on the 24" long 3/8" drive extension.

Note these items when pressing the backup ring and cylinder end seal:

Keep the tool straight to avoid damaging the cylinder wall. Check the tool angle, and correct it if necessary, when removing the backup ring and cylinder end seal. Use a press to remove the backup ring and cylinder end seal. Do not try to remove the backup ring and cylinder end seal by striking the tool; striking the tool would break the backup ring and cylinder end seal, and the backup ring and cylinder end seal would remain in the gearbox housing.

![](images/76e1d9e1327366c2a666a2fa571a1eb61239d8e1d49c7b296f3ee249ac183e21.webp)


### Steering Gearbox Overhaul (cont'd)

23. Wrap vinyl tape (A) over the splines on the pinion shaft.

![](images/6f78f2cde8cec17df19e7b0fec96edafaf0bb0421cf16caa082ee1f4b76c6b01.webp)

24. Separate the valve housing (A) from the pinion shaft/sleeve (B) and the valve oil seal (C).

![](images/ad2ad183902bbd11ac2721271b529cecc9556006fd7a5a6e00536facb2353887.webp)

25. With your finger, check the inner wall of the valve housing where the seal ring slides. If there is a step in the wali, the housing is worn, replace it.

![](images/674cd5e8c01841d0a722fc0a8e2f0c0e8f48b210aee33e20d693d2d9bb6ff503.webp)

26. Check for wear, burrs, and other damage to the edges of the grooves in the sleeve.

NOTE: The pinion shaft and sleeve are a precision matched set. If either the pinion shaft or sleeve must be replaced, replace both parts as a set.

![](images/740559230c516688565b422df04a272e09bda0064044f3a60de4f67887cf7dd0.webp)

27. Remove the snap ring (A) and the sleeve (B) from the pinion shaft (C).

![](images/bad1cbf249b9eebd6a4083a132ed1126507de2faa70cb617223944d948daccec.webp)

28. Using a cutter or an equivalent tool, cut and remove the seal rings (A) from the sleeve. Be careful not to damage the edges of the sleeve grooves and outer surface when removing the seal rings.

![](images/31bcb51bb75533d21796f3ad1b6906f6388cf957076bbcb0339948aa5dc4524d.webp)

29. Using a cutter or an equivalent tool, cut the valve seal ring (A) and O-ring (B) at the cutting groove position (C) in the pinion shaft. Remove the valve seal ring and O-ring. Be careful not to damage the edges of the pinion shaft groove and outer surface when removing the valve seal ring and O-ring.

![](images/082dbc37d22c00d8df77d391e58be69c9fbcc9cba7706510aa45e373156e516a.webp)

30. Remove the valve oil seal (A) and roller bearing (B) out of the valve housing using a hydraulic press and an appropriate size socket (C).

![](images/34614fd2447d7478b3584cf067b3e4a48047df2e47f1218bdbcebdf5a1296cd8.webp)

31. Clean the disassembled parts with solvent, and dry them with compressed air. Do not dip rubber parts in the solvent.


### Reassembly

32. Wrap vinyl tape (A) over the splines and stepped portion of the shaft, and coat the surface of the vinyl tape with power steering fluid.

![](images/ddb8d5d1cd0897804dd75b1712730f0c266b339bae296202f940ac0ed918bdb2.webp)

33. Fit the new O-ring (B) in the groove of the pinion shaft. Then slide the new valve seal ring (C) over the shaft and in the groove on the pinion shaft.

34. Remove the vinyl tape, and apply power steering fluid to the surface of the valve seal ring (A).

![](images/56e2f6d0aec63f7db2eec925f8a2bcb45c6530fad5b3a2611893502224a60f26.webp)

35. Apply power steering fluid to the inside of the valve seal ring sizing tool (B). Set the larger diameter end of the sizing tool over the valve seal ring, and move the sizing tool up and down several times to make the valve seal ring fit in the pinion shaft groove.   
36. Remove the sizing tool, turn it over, and slide the smaller diameter end over the valve seal ring. Move it up and down several times to make the valve seal ring fit snugly in the pinion shaft groove.

37. Apply power steering fluid to the surface of the sleeve seal guide (A). Slip two new seal rings (B) over the sleeve seal guide from the smaller diameter end, and expand them. Install only two rings at a time from each end of the pinion shaft sleeve (C).

Note these items when installing the seal ring:

Do not over-expand the seal ring. Install the resin seal rings with care so as not to damage them. After installation, make sure you contract the seal rings using the sizing tool.   
There are two types of sleeve seal rings; black and brown. Do not mix the different types of rings as they are not compatible.

![](images/50968f5e5d67dc2893a95da1afe16b8f7fb4ff081c31c9d1b96c00f457a908cf.webp)

38. Align the ring guide with each groove in the sleeve, and slide a sleeve seal ring into each groove. After instalation, compress the seal rings with your fingers temporarily.

39. Apply power steering fluid to the seal rings on the sleeve, and to the entire inside surface of the sizing tool (A), then slowly insert the sleeve into the sizing tool.

![](images/070876464ddfd786bc80673e2bc7d3beaa426a982906462e4f13ef327131dc04.webp)

40. Move the sleeve back and forth several times to make sure the seal rings fit snugly in the sleeve. Make sure the seal rings are not twisted, and contract the seal rings.

41.Apply power steering fluid to the surface of the pinion shaft A) Slide the sleeve  onto he pinion shat y aligning the locating pin () on the pinion shaft with the cutout (D) in the sleeve. Then install the new snap ring (E) securely in the pinion shaft groove. Be careful not to damage the valve seal ring when installing the sleeve.

![](images/1bb3e3477354fc62530cf229da74a79445d5a0db25f9c9d6149eef2d454ce126.webp)

42. Apply power steering fluid to the seal ring lip of the .new valve oil seal (A), then install the seal in the valve housing (B) using a hydraulic press, bearing driver attachment (C), and driver handle (D). Install the seal with its grooved side facing the tool.

![](images/d5c64f7b0cfff1c4d5cb242c10e1c001f8ca5380615f2164518090aee8aaed8f.webp)

43. Press the new roller bearing (E) into the valve housing with a hydraulic press, attachment, and driver handle. 44. Wrap vinyl tape (A) over the pinion shaft/sleeve (B), then coat the vinyl tape with power steering fluid.

![](images/8002b6a2a24218118f4abb45b770c9d49bf603fe8cc947004d1a7008a398eab8.webp)

45. Insert the pinion shaft/sleeve into the valve housing (C). Be careful not to damage the valve seal rings (D).

46. Remove the vinyl tape from the pinion shaft, then remove any residue from the tape adhesive.


### Steering Gearbox Overhaul (cont'd)

47. Press the new valve oil seal (A) into the valve housing with a hydraulic press, bearing driver attachment (B), and oil seal driver (C). Check that the pinion shaft/sleeve turns smoothly by hand after installing it.

![](images/1cb27b7de9355c446d5506b0e4444099a690d2bdf44861687d463dd47588c97e.webp)

48. Coat the piston seal ring guide with power steering fluid, then slide it onto the rack, big end first.

49. Position the new O-ring (A) and new piston seal ring (B) on the piston seal ring guide (C), then slide them down toward the big end of the tool.

Note these items during reassembly:

Do not over expand the resin seal rings. Install the resin seal rings with care so as not to damage them. After installation, make sure you contract the seal ring using the sizing tool. Replace the piston's O-ring and seal ring as a set.

![](images/75a4ea9f9c8e2996e544b6e6fe30c60993e268d9f4481a3895ce7590f8bd8b95.webp)

50. Pull the O-ring off into the piston groove, then pull the piston seal ring offinto the piston groove on top of the O-ring.

51. Coat the piston seal ring (A) and the inside of the sizing tool (B) with power steering fluid, then carefully slide the tool onto the rack and over the piston seal ring.

![](images/fc81fbf30d849675963bb4c293e4cbabd9cdc502ad87f42f708cfbe1b8ae158c.webp)

52. Move the sizing tool back and forth several times to make the piston seal ring seats snugly in groove of the piston.   
53. Wrap vinyl tape around the rack teeth and rack end edges, make sure that the vinyl tape is wrapped carefully so that there is no stepped portion.

![](images/f8d9b8812279bc3381fb831203e203a6341f6733296104a31a6efba84e5e4423.webp)

54. Coat the inside surface of the new cylinder end seal (A) with power steering fluid, then install it onto the steering rack with its grooved side toward the piston. When installing the cylinder end seal, be careful not to damage the lip of the seal with the edges or teeth of the steering rack.

![](images/a746ab7ffc3d9e15ff6e0fe5a8c55583bf51f2006e10a1bae21cba2ba3ed3fa6.webp)

57. Apply steering grease to the steering rack teeth, then insert the steering rack into the gearbox housing. Be careful not to damage the inner surface of the cylinder wall with the rack edges.

![](images/49d08849346c0f027fdfa9f4facb3f7c39350bcd8ad8c9df9ebcfd3312d637cc.webp)

58. Insert an appropriate size socket (A) onto the steering rack as shown.

55. Remove the vinyl tape from the steering rack, then remove any adhesive residue.

56. Install the new backup ring (A) on the steering rack, then place the backup ring and cylinder end seal (B) against the piston (C).

![](images/5c2cc80e9cddd5914bdc29548644463cc2c4f9a50f0c5b126c334af6c6ed9213.webp)

![](images/555b4e3fdf8261696e82a6f7f1ffa419892da77593a9e9b8710f439baee66f9d.webp)

59. Install the new backup ring (B) and new cylinder end seal (C) into the bottom of the cylinder by pressing on the tool with a press. Do not push on the tool with excessive force as it may damage the backup ring and cylinder end seal.

60. Remove the tool, and center the steering rack.


### Steering Gearbox Overhaul (cont'd)

61. Coat the inside surface of the new cylinder end seal (A) and steering rack with power steering fluid, then install the cylinder end seal onto the steering rack with its grooved side toward the cylinder.

![](images/a2923b743ab1478c00e03d97d21fe1c8e7e07c900a910ade4157afaf47e51d3f.webp)

62. Push in the cylinder end seal with your finger. Be careful not to damage the surface of the seal with the threads and burrs at the staked position of the cylinder housing.   
63. Hold the gearbox housing using a C-clamp (A) and wooden blocks (B) to a work bench as shown. Do not clamp the cylinder part of the gearbox housing in a vise.

г

64. Coat the inside surface of the cylinder end (A) with power steering fluid, then install the cylinder end by screwing it into the cylinder (B). Tighten the cylinder end to the specified torque.

![](images/a340d7dca0e3d132ec7b2a71300006872f4345fcb7818384951c79ce1834f930.webp)

65. Stake the point of the cylinder shown (opposite from where the stake was removed during disassembly).   
66. Coat the new O-ring (A) with steering grease, and carefully fit it on the valve housing.

![](images/c45999238dbb0eeb29b15ffcf6f4f85047c6fdbc8e4b753b4bab15705e14fe25.webp)

67. Apply steering grease to the ball bearing (B) in the gearbox housing, then install the valve body unit (C) by engaging the gears. Note the valve body unit installation position (direction of the line connections).

68. Loosely install the flange bolts (D).

69. Install cylinder line A and B to the steering gearbox.

Note these items during reassembly:

Thoroughly clean the joints of the cylinder lines. The joints must be free of foreign material. Install the cylinder lines by tightening the flare nuts by hand first, then tighten the flare nuts to the specified torque.

![](images/505fa45df5f7aef8897fef2fa251ffd99d62092ce0145f11538fc2f1f4da8fe2.webp)

70. Apply steering grease to the sliding surface of the rack guide (A), and install t onto the gearbox housing.

![](images/48a0fd52f086e59a37915116bc22a3e1e7280b9d2ba687ba8da52a2ea77f7c5b.webp)

71. Remove the old sealant from the rack guide screw (B), then apply new sealant (Three Bond 1215 or Loctite 5699) to the middle of the threads. Install the spring (C), the disc washer (D), the rack guide screw, and locknut (E).

NOTE: If more than 5 minutes have passed after applying the sealant, remove the old sealant and residue, and reapply new sealant.

72. Adjust the rack guide screw (see page 17-17). After adjusting, check that the rack moves smoothly by sliding it right and left.

73. Hold the gearbox housing using a C-clamp (A) and wooden blocks (B) to a work bench as shown. Do not clamp the cylinder part of the gearbox housing in a vise.

![](images/7fb28981a3b87a375ce7c7b31884b4ef67b602619153fd8329aee973e47f4611.webp)

74. Install a new rubber stop (A) and a new lock washer (B). Align the lock washer tabs (C) with the slots (D) on the rack end (E) while holding the lock washer in place.

![](images/9ee7d11c4959e62dc35b9acc06c60b0caaed18b2f591c4cae1d5a2d961078799.webp)

75. Hold the flat surface sections of the steering rack with one wrench, and tighten rack end with another wrench. Be careful not to damage the rack surface with the wrench.


### Steering Gearbox Overhaul (cont'd)

76. Bend the lock washer (A) back against the flat spots on the rack end joint housing.

![](images/a5caa46c9290f41ba678566e5dfbdfff3f30364d9f31cbc17a9fe9a65afd810a.webp)

77. Apply multipurpose grease to the circumference of the rack end joint housing (A).

![](images/1cd15ad01e91cabd02e6949223c8c4156b3fb6e4f3b9e0d199b0d986c27ca3d5.webp)

78. Apply a light coat of silicone grease (P/N 08798-9013) to the boot grooves (B) on the rack end. Repeat steps 74 thru 78 for the other side.

NOTE: Make sure not to get any silicone grease on the terminal part of the connectors, especially if you have silicone grease on your hands or gloves.

79. Center the steering rack within its stroke.

80. Install the new self-locking nut (A) onto the pinion shaft end, and tighten to the specified torque.

![](images/13008871f3a32585748caad0a3148e094515aad6d3c831f8d67b2939b03dd563.webp)

81. Remove the old sealant from the threads on the gearbox housing (B), and apply new sealant (Three Bond 1215 or Loctite 5699) al the way around the threads on the gearbox housing and the new end plug (C). Install the end plug onto the gearbox housing, and tighten it to the specified torque. NOTE: If more than 5 minutes have passed after applying the sealant, remove the old sealant and residue, and reapply new sealant.

82. Tighten the flange bolts (A) to the specified torque.

![](images/c264fcbb1817c89012dac8036eb5798b488384d3f52a5a4bb3e4e8fe86a92702.webp)  
20 N·m (2.0 kgf•m, 15 lbfft)

83. After tightening, use a drift to stake (A) the gearbox housing shoulder against the end plug (B).

86. Install the new boot band (A) by aligning the tabs (B) with the holes (C) on the band.

![](images/a2d390146b00e1fc21666e17c1cbf8607c155272ca0fb84fe9054abd83a8d0d9.webp)

84. Clean off any grease or contamination from the boot instalation groove (A) around the gearbox housing. Install the boot (B) on the rack end with the tie-rod clip (C), and fit the boot end in the installation groove in the housing properly.

87. Close the ear portion (A) of the boot band (B) with commercially available pincers Oetiker 1098 (C) or equivalent.

![](images/fbcf70ccb3bddc9b4670dfd9ee2287ffbcd9a981059acd81696b7ebede721bdb.webp)

![](images/a99bbe578277a9599233d4a5bf92c14b2b728c42ab62aa0812d9f0ddcdf0b8eb.webp)

85. After installing the boot, wipe the grease off the threaded section (D) of the rack end.

![](images/1ccfb21f04bb34c618afc856474b57eda662fae898c8829e5ad914863acb6f5b.webp)

88. Slide the rack right and left to be certain that the boots are not deformed or twisted. Repeat steps 84 thru 88 for the other side.

89. Install both tie-rod ends to the rack ends.

90. Install the steering gearbox (see page 17-64).


### Special Tools Required

Subframe Adapter VSB02C000016\* •Subframe Alignment Pin 070AG-SJAA10S \*: Available through the Honda Tool and Equipment Program, 888-424-6857.

1. Before installing the steering gearbox, make sure that no power steering fluid is on the mating surface of the steering gearbox and the front subframe. To prevent the gearbox mounting bolts from loosening after the installation, remove any power steering fluid from the mount cushions and the bolt holes.

2. Wrap vinyl tape over the splines on the pinion shaft (A).

![](images/25af98a2bc5669381b8b939c703c3979a19a814f495c54c8ad995ae06557d67a.webp)

3. Install the return joint (B) if removed.

4. Install the pinion shaft grommet (A). Align the slot (B) in the pinion shaft grommet with the lug portion (C) on the valve housing. Make sure there is no gap between the grommet and the valve housing.

![](images/e7ad802db901617f7c518bf75fc62d41c7d13b7c74dc413f501ea9cd6c05af2c.webp)

5. Turn the lip (A) of the pinion shaft grommet.

![](images/c423daf223dade73927ad237dfdb95be760a54c0a11d8dd2dc616fa523eb5695.webp)

6. Slide the steering gearbox (B) between the front subframe and the body from the driver's side. 7. Carefuly move the steering gearbox (A) toward the passenger's side until the pinion shaft clears the fenderwell opening on the body.

![](images/4246c4beafedd2cf482660c794d462e254b396158d06ba066e0aedaa66123f91.webp)

8. Continue moving the steering gearbox toward the passenger's side until the steering gearbox is in position.

9. Install the washers (A), the stiffener plates (B), the new mounting bolts (C), and the flange bolts (D) on the driver's side of the gearbox. Then loosely tighten the mounting bolts and the flange bolts.

![](images/4cef215050eb5f9e098263a239d3a0eeb586e5a5305bb918d69b14eeb2c69fdd.webp)

10. Position the cutout (A) of the mounting cushion (B) as shown, and install it on the passenger's side of the steering gearbox.

![](images/5682df02b94167d58d9321b0f1c1d8797497b06a32c698334b0abb2b687db308.webp)

11. Install the gearbox mounting bracket (C) over the mounting cushion, and tighten the flange bolts (D) to the specified torque.   
12. Tighten the mounting bolts and the flange bolts on the driver's side of the steering gearbox to the specified torque alternately in two steps.

13. Loosely tighten the new right rear subframe mounting bolt (A) and the new stiffener mounting bolt (B); insert the subframe alignment pin (C) through the positioning slot (D) on the rear stiffener, through the positioning hole (E) on the front subframe, and into the positioning hole (F) on the body, then tighten the right rear subframe mounting bolt.

![](images/40cd835b6d1cdeacb2380a8688b4ea10dba25dffed40ceb6bce28a6b15e10938.webp)

14. Loosely tighten the new left rear subframe mounting bolt and the new stiffener mounting bolt with the same procedure as the right rear using the subframe alignment pin.

15. Loosely tighten the new subframe mounting bolt (A) and the stiffener mounting bolt (B) to both front stiffeners (C).

![](images/2275a357e0edce3da1b853d7b155520e3c21b2707175873f31af6e2a3fb6a759.webp)

20. Install the flange nuts (A) to the lower transmission mount, and tighten them to the specified torque.

![](images/08dbd5d1c5d88959232b269219dc67797552997dcc409d4eaa84ac30281cdfab.webp)

42. Install the rear engine mount actuator harness clip (A) to the stiffener plate (B) on the driver's side of the steering gearbox.

![](images/57bab9d20e1ae3f571822d4e743066e5bf89758b1eb41e114b4e9a0ffcf5d754.webp)

43. Connect the rear engine mount actuator connector (A).

![](images/3eeadde41c7979041d687de041767b655d0cd2c5e80b991c214a8bc7cbe64f0b.webp)


### Steering Gearbox Installation (cont'd)

44. Tighten the new front engine mount bolt (A), then install the front engine mount stop (B).

![](images/3339fa6a29d1303f91fa17f578133141c0bd6b473f18ba3bdd9c15a4b680e58e.webp)

45. Remove the engine support hanger, the engine hanger balance bar, and the hanger adapter set.   
46. Install the harness clamp bracket (A) to the rear cylinder head.

![](images/d2cb34db549b5bbb045bf56ea091a6d39b302a740fe4d6344399cf6d043c46f3.webp)

8 x1.25 mm   
22 N·m (2.2 kgfm, 16 lbf.ft)

47. Install the connector bracket (A) to the front cylinder head.

![](images/7d100209a24643f708cac7a64c56b9df54410a303717b2099e3bca4511afc86a.webp)

48.Tighten the rear engine mount mounting bolts to the specified torque. 49. Instal the power steering heat shield (A) with the flange bolts, and tighten them to the specified torque.

![](images/3cbc6746a63db2b5e9aa02e64c4d40b8408ef06ea630e0534ada90286de6cf03.webp)

50. Install the pump outlet hose bracket bolt (A).

![](images/08b2c575f08aa1b1fa2b7f6a7bc69879925ef41747b04df9de0261f45fa27c59.webp)

51. Install the strut brace (see page 20-261).

52. Install the front grille cover (see page 20-230).

53. Install the engine cover (see step 1 on page 4-20).

54. Place a floor jack under the lower arm, and raise the suspension to load it with the vehicle's weight. Do not place the jack against the ball joint pin of the knuckle.

55. Tighten the damper fork mounting nut while holding the mounting bolt to the specified torque (see step 23).

56. Install the front wheels, then set the wheels in the straight ahead position.

NOTE: Before installing the wheel, clean the mating surfaces between the brake disc and the inside of the wheel.

57. Center the steering rack within its stroke.

58. Remove the steering wheel holder tool (A).

59. Loosen the steering joint upper bolt (A), and slip the lower end of the steering joint (B) onto the pinion shaft (C) taking care to align the gap (D) within the angle.

NOTE: Pick up the tabs (E) of the pinion shaft grommet, and turn up the lip of the pinion shaft grommet securely in place. Make sure that light does not enter from the space between the pinion shaft grommet and the body.

![](images/d3ecff6705a8fff8899b95761ff771e23ce0cfc454e47e83b8d9133e50367b9d.webp)

60. Align the bolt hole (A) on the steering joint with the groove (B) around the pinion shaft, then loosely install the steering joint lower bolt (C). Be sure that the joint bolt is securely in the groove in the pinion shaft.

![](images/d697a0bebcf0d6227d14b6e29e757184067bfec76f6cdf96b66abc0747d17f7c.webp)

![](images/c1ec2c5d1f260e069b376c475213ac80dd7263076f40831fcfd40f550efc1a6a.webp)

61. Pull on the steering joint to make sure that the steering joint is fully seated, then tighten the steering joint lower bolt to the specified torque.   
62. Tighten the steering joint upper bolt (D) to the specified torque.


### Steering Gearbox Installation (cont'd)

63. Install the steering joint cover (A).

![](images/5fb6e880f7d0123b468125cebc61340fad42f0e3ea100a0b80c1cec51b07a534.webp)

68. After installation, check these items:

Start the engine, allow it to idle, and turn the steering wheel from lock to lock several times to warm up the fluid. Check the gearbox for leaks (see page 17-27).   
Check the steering wheel spoke angle.   
If steering spoke angles to the right and left are not equal (steering wheel and rack are not centered), correct the engagement of the joint/pinion shaft serrations.   
Set the steering column to the center tilt position, and to the center telescopic position, then do the front toe inspection (see page 18-5).

64. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86), and check these items:

Make sure the horn and turn signal switches work properly.   
Make sure the steering wheel switches work properly.

65. Fillthe system with power steering fluid, and bleed air from the system (see page 17-28).

66. Reinstall the driver's side hood support strut bracket (A) with the bolts to proper locations.

![](images/d57e7c4de645e09e0889f3afb7aedf137441b494534bc0e5a76c7e90052e24ad.webp)

67. Reáttach the passenger's side hood support strut on the pivot bolt (see page 20-212).
