### Airbag and Tensioner Disposal

Special Tools Required Deployment Tool 07AAZ-000A100

Before scrapping any front airbags, side airbags, side curtain airbags, or front seat belt tensioners (including those in a whole vehicle to be scrapped), the part(s) must be deployed. If the vehicle is still within the warranty period, the Honda District Parts and Service Manager must give approval and/or special instruction before deploying the part(s). Only after the part(s) have been deployed (as the result of vehicle collision, for example), can they be scrapped. If the parts appear intact (not deployed), treat them with extreme caution. Follow this procedure.


### Deploying Airbags in the Vehicle

If an SRS equipped vehicle is to be entirely scrapped, its front airbags, side airbags, side curtain airbags, and front seat belt tensioners should be deployed while still in the vehicle. These parts should not be considered as salvageable parts and should never be installed in another vehicle.

1. Turn the ignition switch to LOCK (0). Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work.   
2. Confirm that each front airbag, side airbag, side curtain airbag, or front seat belt tensioner is securely mounted.   
3. Confirm that the deployment tool is functioning properly by following the check procedure on the tooi label.


### Driver's Airbag

4. Remove the access panel (A) from the steering wheel, then disconnect the driver's airbag inflator 4P connector (B) on the cable reel harness.

![](images/6d117338a8b753bdfc3174fcf65c0b5ddba2fbd60aa5565a362e8be1b47e692d.webp)


### Side Curtain Airbag

5. Open the glove box. Disconnect the glove box damper from the pivot on the glove box (see step 1 on page 20-143), then lower the glove box. 6. Detach the connector clip (A), then disconnect the front passenger's airbag inflator 4P connector (B) on the dashboard wire harness.

![](images/5884fd8ca3e67b81bc196393d51e461129268ecac526399f0f2c9a4f690cfabd.webp)


### Side Airbag

7. Disconnect the driver's and the front passenger's side airbag inflator 2P connectors (A) on the SRS floor wire harness.

8. Remove the headliner (see page 20-109).

9. Disconnect the left and right side curtain airbag inflator 2P connectors (A) on the SRS floor wire harness.

![](images/e2e24a60964e60d62989e839e3e6a96b1387dee4836f9debf623a16a6b0fa59b.webp)


### Front Seat Belt Tensioner

10. Remove the B-pillar lower trim (see page 20-92).

11. Disconnect the driver's and the front passenger's seat belt tensioner 4P connectors (A) on the SRS floor wire harness. Pull the front seat belt out all the way and cut it.

![](images/1d15965b5b11168d3438922ba5855a8ef384f1fd1db56208ee06c219e2a9be31.webp)

![](images/df9eee413b934262bb125e102c6509a8ca1060c08e0187f71f8088d024f4b6d8.webp)


### Airbag and Tensioner Disposal (cont'd)

12. Cut off each connector, and strip the ends of the wires. Twist each pair of unlike colored wires together, and clip an alligator clip (A) from the deployment tool to each pair.


> ℹ️ **Примечание:** 
> Place the deployment tool at least 10m (33 ft)away from the vehicle.   
> The driver's and front passenger's airbags have dual inflators. Twist each pair of unlike colored wires together, and clip an alligator clip to each pair.
>
> ![](images/616b998c3fa353f9e4b2910d0d2fadc9fe4545f7ee07bb6e2d21ab6906f9bd35.webp)
>
> '07AAZ-000A100
>
> ![](images/df2851a5b8911a54a475c401c862726494c9aee72952aed2edcbb1841f97ead8.webp)
>
> 13. Connect a 12 volt battery to the tool.
>
> If the green light on the tool comes on, the igniter circuit is defective and cannot deploy the component. Go to Disposal of Damaged Components.   
> If the red light on the tool comes on, the component is ready to be deployed.
>
> 14. Push the tool's deployment switch. The airbags and tensioners should deploy (deployment is both highly audible and visible: A loud noise and rapid inflation of the bag, followed by slow deflation). If the components deploy and the green light on the tool comes on, continue with this procedure. If a component does not deploy, and the green light comes on, its igniter is defective. Go to Disposal of Damaged Components. During deployment, the airbags can become hot enough to burn you. Wait for 30 minutes after deployment before touching the airbags.
>
> 15. Dispose of the complete airbag or tensioner. No part of it can be reused. Place it in a sturdy plastic bag (A), and seal it securely. Dispose of the deployed airbag according to your local regulations.
>
> ![](images/07fa969f35102d83c75c60a6efbfecd535eebfbf07896bfb088c74f8c912abfe.webp)


### Deploying Components Out of the Vehicle Disposal of Damaged Components

If an intact airbag or tensioner has been removed from a scrapped vehicle, or has been found defective or damaged during transit, storage, or service, it should be deployed as follows:

![](images/791819671b1904c63bc6332d771fd12800e6966af513b35209964e0ad4580f0a.webp)

1. Confirm that the deployment tool is functioning properly by following the check procedure Deploying Airbags in the Vehicle on the tool label. 2. Position the airbag face up, outdoors, on flat ground, at least 10 m (33 ft) from any obstacles or people. 3. Follow steps 12 through 15 of the Deploying Airbag in the Vehicle.

NOTE: The driver's and front passenger's airbags have dual inflators. Twist each pair of unlike colored wires together, and clip an alligator clip to each pair.

1. If installed in a vehicle, follow the removal procedure for the driver's airbag (see page 24-184), the front passenger's airbag (see page 24-185), the side airbag (see page 24-188), the side curtain airbag (see page 24-190), and the front seat belt tensioner (see page 24-4).

2. In all cases, make a short circuit by cutting, stripping, and twisting together the two inflator wires.

NOTE: The driver's and front passenger's airbags have dual inflators. The like color wires go to the individual inflators. Twist the like colored wires together.

3. Package the component in exactly the same packaging that the new replacement part came in.

4. Mark the outside of the box DAMAGED AIRBAG NOT DEPLOYED, DAMAGED SIDE AIRBAG NOT DEPLOYED, DAMAGED SIDE CURTAIN AIRBAG NOT DEPLOYED, or DAMAGED SEAT BELT TENSIONER NOT DEPLOYED so it does not get confused with your parts stock.

5. Contact your Honda District Parts and Service Manager for instructions on how and where to return it for disposal.


### Deployment Tool Check

1. Connect the yellow clips to both switch protector handles on the tool.   
2. Then connect the red lead to the positive battery post and the black lead to the negative battery post.   
3. Push the operation switch: The green light should come on, indicating that the tool is operating properly and is ready for use. If the red light stays on, the tool is faulty, and another one must be used for the procedure.   
4. Disconnect the tool clips and connectors from the protector handles and the battery.


### Removal

1. Set the front wheels in the straight ahead position. 2. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work. 3. Remove the driver's airbag (see page 24-184). 4. Disconnect cable reel connector C (20P) on the cable reel subharness from the cable reel (A).

![](images/1576f9354c5c767665c5168d2c5d0aff7e1e689c828d47122c24523bf0b3985d.webp)

5. Loosen the steering wheel bolt (B) three turns. 6. Install a commercially available steering wheel puller on the steering wheel (see step 5 on page 17-7). 7. Remove the steering wheel puller, then remove the steering wheel bolt and steering wheel from the steering column.

8. Remove the upper and lower column covers (see page 20-151).   
9. Disconnect cable reel connector B (4P) on the dashboard wire harness and cable reel connector A (20P) on the dashboard wire harness from the cable reel (C).

![](images/2bea1b57910cb5e4452d1f2c2bc485858b1dcb9da5b42a93f0d790dcee934c5a.webp)

10. Release the upper lock tab (A) under the cable reel connector with a 90 ° hook shaped tool (B). Slide the tool below the cable reel connector just above the lock tab. Release the lower lock tab (C), and slide the cable reel off the column.

![](images/696ff0a70a9c7b572f7acc581778fa79151e1b9575c3ae2e34e4501da1dc7d6f.webp)


### Installation

1. Before installing the steering wheel, make sure the front wheels are aligned straight ahead. 2. Set the turn signal canceling sleeve (A) so that the projections (B) are aligned vertically.

![](images/e7c669b1925059f627492e2bb8edc9a77b0303b0eaa723e297aed96b991892f2.webp)

3. Carefully install the cable reel (C) on the steering column shaft. Then connect cable reel connector A (20P) on the dashboard wire harness and cable reel connector B (4P) on the dashboard wire harness to the cable reel.

![](images/c91889234a59cdc95f100725e64fb31f6f135882276b9a3a22220bece61d8be0.webp)


### Cable Reel Replacement (cont'd)

4. Install the upper and lower column covers (see page 20-151).

5. Before installing the steering wheel, make sure the front wheels are pointing straight ahead, then center the cable reel (A). Do this by first rotating the cable reel clockwise until it stops. Then rotate it counterclockwise about three full turns. The arrow mark (B) on the cable reel label should point straight up.

![](images/cf6eb07d87c82c028ee99322834e446f26076b0b8edad4faf9a9fb55485b1afb.webp)

6. Position the two tabs (A) of the turn signal canceling sleeve (B) as shown. Install the steering wheel on to the steering column shaft, making sure the steering wheel hub (C) engages the pins (D) of the cable reel and tabs of the turn signal canceling sleeve. Do not tap on the steering wheel or steering column shaft when installing the steering wheel.

![](images/cb8fad3e9939b6533c785a31e1daf01c5dcaf47d6298d4cdec1b1d3376f67b23.webp)

7. Install the steering wheel bolt (A), and tighten it to the specified torque. Connect the cable reel connector C (20P) on the cable reel subharness to the cable reel (B). Make sure the wire harness is routed and fastened properly.

![](images/dac5342cc1ed3fa859c64c12967962baad4d27136bcc5c8d48bb8762ff1d6ee5.webp)

8. Install the driver's airbag (see page 24-184).

9. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86).

10. Clear any DTCs with the HDS (see page 24-27).

11. After installing the cable reel, confirm proper system operation:

Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds and then goes off.   
Make sure the horn and turn signal switches works properly.   
Make sure the steering wheel switches works properly.   
Make sure the horn works properly.

12. After installation, check the steering wheel spoke angle. If the steering spoke angles to the right and left are not equal (steering wheel is not centered), correct the engagement of the wheel/column shaft splines.


### Removal

1. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work.   
2. Remove the driver's and passenger's dashboard center lower covers (see page 20-138).   
3. Remove the clips (A), then remove the left and right heater ducts (B, C).

![](images/a5e2f795a6ef8c03ac659194f50ea9075f1a23d1e7df400d1210b75ffa27033d.webp)

4. Disconnect SRS unit connectors A (39P) and B (39P) from the SRS unit (C).

7. Remove the SRS unit (B) from the driver's side.


### Installation

1. Install the SRS unit (A) with the new TORX bolt (B) using a TORX T30 bit.

NOTE: Be sure the SRS unit is sitting squarely against it's bracket before torquing the TORX bolt.

![](images/a496599841d34c9cec7a7dc3dd8117499286a3334edda41c0678e1c8998d7d90.webp)

11Nm (1.1 kgf.m, 8 lbfft) Replacee.

3. Connect the SRS connectors A (39P) and B (39P) to the SRS unit (C); push them into position until they click and the lever locks are fully secured (see page 24-21).

![](images/3ad2442d3e12aa0b1db0e121d7a6213382f3b4c61ff9f4e04919b4df60c7d496.webp)

6. Make sure the SRS unit has the latest software. If it does not have the latest, update the software in the SRS unit (see page 24-28).   
7. Do the ODS unit initialization (see page 24-29).   
8. Check the operation of the ODS unit with the HDS (see page 24-31).   
9. Confirm proper SRS operation: Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds and then goes off.

10. Reinstall all removed parts.

2.Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86).

> 1. Do the battery terminal disconnction procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work.

> 2. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86).   
> 3. Clear any DTCs with the HDS (see page 24-27).

4. Confirm proper SRS operation: Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds and then goes off.   
5. Reinstall all removed parts.


### Installation

1. Raise the driver's seat all the way up. 2. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work. 3. Remove the driver's seat (see page 20-165). 4. Disconnect the driver's seat position sensor 2P connector (A) on the driver's seat wire harness.

![](images/a4b8a885b8b968415be2d983e3594d8c92ca0771b5e217443f6097374e6a8c9d.webp)

5. Remove the nut (B), then remove the driver's seat position sensor (C).

NOTE: Be sure to install the harness so it does not pinched or interfere with other parts.

1. Install the driver's seat position sensor (A) with the new nut (B), then connect the driver's seat position sensor 2P connector (C) on the driver's seat wire harness.

![](images/dbb9febd3441713c79dd5d3a7eeebf19ff982a282d4fac83bfbc9c67851b61a4.webp)

2. Install the driver's seat (see page 20-165). 3. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86). 4. Clear any DTCs with the HDS (see page 24-27). 5. Check the operation of the driver's seat position sensor with the HDS (see page 24-33). 6. Confirm proper SRS operation: Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator comes on for about 6 seconds and then goes off.


### Passenger's Airbag Cutoff Indicator Replacement

1. Do the battery terminal disconnection procedure (see page 22-86), then wait at least 3 minutes before starting work.   
2. With navigation: Remove the dashboard center vent (see step 1 on page 20-148).   
3. Without navigation: Remove the audio switch panel (see page 23-131).   
4. Disconnect the hazard warning switch/passenger's airbag cutoff indicator 6P connector (A) on the audio wire harness.


### With navigation

![](images/0dcc431e49cdf3380bf0b3e630eb194c4dbef27613ab625c6c2e66cda69117e3.webp)  
Without navigation

![](images/c7d2cbfd0a0f420b1b727d0578a6735e6db3c68c12496dba5dbb12e9c2400195.webp)

5. Push out the hazard warning switch/passenger's airbag cutoff indicator (B) from behind the dashboard center vent (C) or audio switch panel (D).

6. Reinstall the parts in the reverse order of removal. 7. Do the battery terminal reconnection procedure (see page 22-86). 8. Clear any DTCs with the HDS (see page 24-27). 9. Confirm proper SRS operation: Turn the ignition switch to ON (Il), and check that the SRS indicator and the passenger's airbag cutoff indicator comes on for about 6 seconds and then goes off.
